meaning_en: The root رعد (raʿada) primarily describes the sky thundering before rain. Tropically, it means to threaten or menace someone with evil.
The root صبع primarily refers to a finger or toe. It can metaphorically describe an "imprint" of goodness or influence, as in God's favor or a shepherd's care for his flock.
The root "sfk" primarily means to shed or pour forth liquids, especially blood or tears. It can also tropically refer to speaking profusely or rapidly.
The primary meaning of حطط (HTT) is to lower, put down, or cause something to descend. It implies a reduction in height, status, or quantity, often with the sense of unloading or diminishing.
The root غلف (ghalafa) primarily means to put something into a sheath or cover, like a knife into its scabbard. It also describes applying perfume or ointment, especially to the beard.
The root زحزح (zHzH) primarily means to move or remove something from its place, to push it away, or to cause it to recede.
The word "كَهْرَبٌ" (kahrab) refers to yellow amber. Its origin is Persian, meaning "straw-attracting," due to its electrostatic properties. This term is the root of the modern word "electricity."
The root صبغ primarily means to dye or color something, like cloth or hair, altering its appearance. It also extends to dipping or immersing things, such as hands in water or food in sauce.
The root جَنَفَ (janafa) means to incline, deviate, or act wrongfully, especially in speech or affairs. It implies straying from the right path, like in making an unjust will.
The root "rfth" primarily refers to foul, unseemly, or lewd speech, especially concerning women or sexual matters.
The root خيط (khyT) primarily refers to a thread or string, used for sewing.
The root LDD primarily signifies intense contention, dispute, or obstinacy. It describes someone who is vehemently argumentative, quarrelsome, or stubbornly persistent in their opposition.
The root أمو (Amw) primarily refers to a female slave or handmaid. It is the opposite of a free woman. The word has several plural forms, with إِمَآءٌ being the most common.
The root HyD primarily describes a woman's menstruation, the flow of blood from her womb.
The root عضل (EDl) primarily means to prevent or withhold, especially a woman from marrying, often wrongfully. It also describes someone becoming muscular or brawny.
The root ج س م (jsm) primarily relates to the body or form. It can describe something taking shape or embodying a quality.
The root كرس (krs) primarily refers to a throne, chair, or seat. It can also metaphorically signify dominion, God's power, or knowledge.
The root مَحَقَ (maḥaqa) means to diminish, deprive of blessing, or completely obliterate something, leaving no trace. It implies a total doing away with.
The root رَسَخَ (raskha) means to be firm, steady, or fixed in place. It describes something deeply rooted, like knowledge in the heart or ink on paper.
The root كهل (khl) refers to the upper back or shoulder area. It can mean the withers of an animal, the part of the back near the neck, or the area between the shoulder blades.
The root كمه (kmh) describes land that is covered or concealed, similar to how clouds obscure the sky. It refers to ground that is hidden from view, perhaps by vegetation or other features.
The root شفو (shfw) primarily means the "edge," "verge," or "brink" of something, like a pit.
The root حفر primarily means "to dig" or "excavate." It can also describe a torrent furrowing a valley or a rain of unknown extent. Figuratively, it means to search into an affair or to emaciate.
The root خبل (khbl) primarily means to be or become corrupted, unsound, or disordered, especially in one's reason, leading to possession or insanity.
The root عَضَضَ (ʿaḍaḍa) primarily means to bite or to seize with the teeth. It can also imply holding on firmly or clinging to something, often with a sense of regret or strong attachment.
The root نمل (nml) refers to the fingertip, specifically the end joint where the nail is located. It can also denote any joint or articulation of the fingers.
The root كبت (kbt) primarily means to throw someone down prostrate, especially on their face, or to repel and abase an enemy. It also signifies God's act of disappointing or causing someone to fail.
The root قرح (qrH) primarily means to wound or cause a sore. It also describes a horse finishing teething or a she-camel showing signs of pregnancy.
The root "dwl" signifies a turn or change, often from an unfortunate to a good state, like a turn of good fortune. It can also refer to a turn in wealth or war, where one party prevails over another.
The root مَحَصَ (mHS) means to purify or clear something, like refining gold from impurities. In a spiritual sense, it refers to God purifying believers or purging sins.
The root كين (kyn) is related to the root سكن (skn), meaning to be still or quiet. It also connects to كون (kwn), which implies existence or being.
The root نعس (n-'-s) primarily describes drowsiness or the beginning of sleep, often likened to a dog's constant dozing.
The root نِحْلَةٌ (niḥlah) refers to an obligation or a religious belief/creed. It's used to ask about someone's religion, as in "What is your religion?"
The root خدن (khdn) refers to a close friend, often a secret or private one. It can imply an amorous or sensual relationship, especially when referring to a female companion.
The root غوط (gwT) primarily refers to a wide, depressed piece of ground or land, often with surrounding inclines. It can also denote a valley.
The root طعن (TEn) primarily means to pierce or stab with a spear. It extends to include verbal attacks, like blaming or censuring someone.
The root شيد (shyd) primarily refers to something plastered with gypsum or built with it. It can also mean raised high or made lofty.
The root QWT relates to sustenance and power. A "Muqīt" is one who provides nourishment, preserves, guards, or protects. It can also mean a witness or one who is acquainted with something.
The root ركس (rks) means to turn something over, upside down, or reverse it. In the Quran, it describes God subverting or causing people to return to disbelief due to their actions.
The root حوذ (Hwdh) primarily means to drive camels, often quickly or forcefully, and by extension, to collect or master something.
The root كسل (ksl) in form IV, أَكْسَلَ عَنْهَا, describes the act of penetration without ejaculation. It implies that one entered but then withdrew without releasing semen.
The root غلو (ghalaw) signifies exceeding limits, being excessive, or immoderate. It applies to actions, prices, and even physical growth.
The root نكف (nkf) primarily means to abstain from or refuse something due to disdain or pride. It implies a sense of haughtiness in declining an action or object.
The root زلم (zlm) primarily refers to divining arrows used by pre-Islamic Arabs to seek guidance. These arrows, called azlām, were marked with commands or prohibitions.
The root خمص (khmS) primarily describes emptiness or hunger, especially of the belly. It can refer to a person who is hungry or lank, and metaphorically, one who abstains from others' possessions.
The root غرو (grw) primarily means to glue or adhere, like skin or fat to a heart. It also describes becoming attached to something, whether out of desire or persistence, such as in anger.
The root W-S-L relates to seeking to get at or obtain something, like water with a bucket. It also means to seek nearness or access to someone, or to gain their favor, by means of something.
Anf (أنف) primarily means "nose." It can also refer to the prominent part or extremity of something, like a mountain or a tooth.
The root همن (hmn) primarily conveys the idea of protecting, guarding, or watching over something.
The root دمع (dmE) primarily describes an eye shedding tears. It can also tropically refer to a wound flowing with blood or a bowl overflowing with grease.
The root حبس (Hbs) primarily means to confine, restrict, or prevent. It signifies holding something back, like detaining a person or restraining an animal.
The root عثر (Ethr) primarily means to stumble or trip, like a person or horse. It can also describe stumbling in speech or lying.
The root قرطس (qrTs) primarily refers to paper or a scroll, often made from papyrus, used for writing. It can also denote a written document or book.
رطب (rTb) describes something moist, fresh, or tender, like fresh produce or a soft branch. It can also metaphorically refer to a supple person or a soft, easy life.
The root ب-ز-غ primarily means "to begin to rise or come forth." It describes the emergence of a tusk or the sun/moon appearing.
The root QDW refers to a pattern, exemplar, or example. It signifies someone or something that is to be imitated. Think of it as a model to follow.
The root صغو (Sgw) primarily means "to incline." It describes physical inclination, like the sun setting or a person leaning.
The root ظفر (zhfr) primarily refers to a nail, talon, or claw, found on humans, animals, and birds. It can also denote a cloven hoof.
The root حوي (Hwy) primarily refers to collecting or gathering things, often by surrounding or encompassing them.
The word "هَلُمَّ" (halumma) means "come." It can be used intransitively, like "come to us," or transitively, like "bring your witnesses." It's a versatile command to approach or bring something.
The root ملق (malaqa) primarily means to behave in a loving, affectionate, or blandishing manner towards someone. It implies coaxing or showing excessive fondness.
The root قيل (qyl) in form X, اِسْتَقاَلَ, means to desire or demand the rescinding of a sale or purchase. It also refers to requesting someone to overlook or forgive a mistake or fault.
The root خصف (khaṣafa) means to sew, patch, or join things together, often by layering. It describes patching a shoe, or Adam and Eve covering themselves with leaves in the Quran.
The root ثعب (thEb) refers to the outflow or outpouring of water. A مثعب (math'ab) is an outlet, channel, or conduit for water, such as from a watering-trough, tank, or rooftop.
The root جرد (jrd) primarily means to strip, bare, or denude, often referring to removing clothes or peeling something.
The root خَوَّارٌ (khawwār) primarily denotes weakness, feebleness, or softness, applied to people (cowardly), spears, arrows, or land.
The root نَصَتَ (naṣata) means to be silent, often with the intention of listening. It can also mean to listen attentively.
The root بَنَن (bnn) primarily refers to the fingertips or the tips of the fingers and toes. It can also denote the extremities or ends of anything.
The root S-D-Y primarily means to turn away or avert one's face, often in disdain or disregard. It can also imply turning aside from a path or purpose.
The root بَطِرَ (baṭira) primarily means to exult excessively, behave insolently, and be ungrateful, often due to wealth. It implies a lack of thankfulness and a turning away from what is right.
The root نكص (nkS) means to recede, retire, or draw back from something, often due to awe or fear. It can also mean to turn back from something one had applied themselves to, especially a good thing.
The root ثخن (thkhn) primarily means to make something thick. Tropically, it refers to rendering someone heavy, weak, or enervated, often through beating or wounds.
The root ألل (All) primarily refers to shining, gleaming, or being bright, like a star or a flame. It can also describe a quick, light movement, or a state of being restless and unable to settle.
The root عيل (Eyl) primarily signifies poverty and want. It also describes something being unattainable or not knowing where to seek something lost.
The fifth form of the root نسأ, "تَنَسَّاَ," is explained by referring to the eighth form. This implies that its meaning or usage is similar to, or derived from, the eighth form of the root.
The root أسس (Ass) primarily means to lay a foundation or to establish something firmly.
The root أوه (Awh) signifies expressions of pain, grief, or lamentation, similar to "Ah!" or "Alas!" It can also convey affection, pity, or impatience.
The root عَزَب (Ezb) primarily refers to something or someone distant, solitary, or apart. It commonly describes a man without a wife or a woman without a husband.
The root بَدَن refers to the body, often excluding the head and limbs, or specifically the torso. It can also denote the main part of a garment, a short coat of mail, or an old mountain goat.
The root غيض (gyD) primarily means for water to decrease, sink into the earth, or disappear. It can also describe anything diminishing, like a flow of milk or a price.
The root جود (jwd) primarily means to be good, excellent, or of high quality. It also signifies generosity, liberality, and giving freely, even to the point of giving one's life.
The root هَرَعَ (haraʿa) primarily means to be driven or urged on, especially with haste and eagerness.
The root سعد (saʿd) signifies good fortune, prosperity, and auspiciousness. It's used for lucky days or stars.
The root شَهَقَ (shhq) primarily means to rise high, like a mountain.
The root جَذَّ (jadhdha) primarily means to cut off or sever something completely and quickly. It implies a decisive and final separation, often leaving no trace or connection behind.
The root جَبَب primarily refers to cutting, severing, or amputating something. It can also describe a well that is lined with stones, or a garment that is cut short.
The root لقط (lqT) refers to something picked up from the ground, often of little value, like lost property, fallen fruit, or gleanings from a harvest.
The root حوش (Hwsh) primarily describes something wild, untamed, or unfamiliar, like a wild animal or an unsociable person.
The root "عجف" (Ejf) primarily describes becoming lean or emaciated, especially for animals.
The root جَهَزَ (jahaza) refers to the essential provisions, equipment, or apparatus needed for a journey, a bride (paraphernalia), or a corpse.
A *ba'īr* is a camel, male or female, like *insān* for humans. It's commonly used for male camels, specifically those in their fifth or ninth year.
The root جزع (jzE) primarily refers to a small quantity or remainder of something, like water in a skin or milk.
The root شَخَصَ (shakhS) primarily means to rise or become elevated. It describes things rising, like stars or arrows, and also refers to eyes becoming fixedly open, often in distress or death.
The root قنع (qnE) refers to a woman's head-covering, specifically one worn over a khimar, or a wider head-covering. It can also denote the pericardium, the integument of the heart.
The root "Sfd" primarily means a bond, shackle, or fetter, often used for captives. It also refers to a gift, metaphorically seen as binding the recipient. The plural is "asfād".
The root "srbl" primarily refers to a shirt or coat of mail, but can also mean any worn garment. The plural "sarābeelu" appears in the Quran.
The root أمل (Aml) primarily means "to hope" or "to expect." It often implies a distant or remote expectation, unlike طمع (tamaʿ), which suggests a near expectation.
The root وسم (wsm) primarily means to mark or put a mark on something, like a garment. It can also mean to brand or stigmatize someone with words or satire.
The root طرو (Trw) primarily describes something being fresh, juicy, or moist, like meat. It can also mean something became new or renewed.
The root مخر (mkhr) primarily describes facing or turning towards the wind, often said of animals like camels or horses.
The root وَصَبَ (w-ṣ-b) primarily means to be constant, continuous, or fixed. It also describes being diseased, ill, or in pain.
The root LBN refers to frankincense, both the tree and its resin. The tree, now identified as Boswellia, produces a resin similar to pistachio nuts.
The root لمح (lmH) primarily means to glance or take a quick, slight look at something, often unawares or from a distance.
The root أثث (athth) primarily refers to household goods, furniture, or possessions. It denotes things that are collected and arranged within a dwelling, making it habitable and comfortable.
The root حظر (Hzhr) primarily means to forbid or prohibit something. It also conveys the sense of debarring or withholding something from others, as if taking it for oneself.
The root كلو (klw) is a variant of كَلَأَ (kalaʾa), meaning to guard, preserve, or protect. It implies watching over something carefully to ensure its safety and well-being.
The root بذر primarily means to sow or scatter seeds, or to scatter things in general. It can also describe God scattering mankind or land putting forth plants.
The root قسطس (qsTs) refers to a balance or weighing instrument, particularly one that is just and accurate.
The root "rft" primarily means to break, crush, or crumble something into pieces, often with one's hand.
The root جلب (jlb) primarily means to drive, bring, or transport something from one place to another, often for trade. It also signifies attracting or procuring something for oneself.
The root "twr" primarily refers to "a time" or "one time," similar to "مره." It can denote a period, whether long or short. The plural forms are "تَارَاتٌ" and "تِيَرٌ.
The root "shakl" refers to likeness, resemblance, or form, like a shape or figure. It also describes a person's particular way of acting, conduct, or nature.

The root نبع (nbE) primarily refers to a specific tree, known for its strong wood. This wood was commonly used for making shafts, such as those for carts, leading to the term نبعان for the two shafts.
The root بَخَعَ (bakh'a) means to slaughter with extreme effectiveness, reaching the back of the neck.
The root جرز (jrz) describes land that is barren, dry, and lacks vegetation. This can be due to a lack of rain, the herbage being cut or eaten, or the land being naturally unproductive.
The root رقد primarily means to sleep, whether by day or night.
The root شَوَى primarily means to roast or broil meat over fire. It implies cooking by direct heat, causing the surface to brown and crisp. The resulting roasted meat is called شِوَاء.

The root HFF primarily means to surround, encompass, or encircle something. It can also imply being light, swift, or having little hair. The core idea often relates to being on all sides of something.
The root زلق (zlq) primarily means to slip or slide, like a foot on a surface or an arrow. It can also describe being disgusted with a place and moving away.
The root هشم (hshm) primarily means to break something, especially if it's dry or hollow, like a head. The verb هَشَّمَهُ (hashshamahu) implies breaking it severely or crushing it.
The root ذرو (dhrw) primarily describes the action of wind raising, scattering, or carrying something away, like dust or grain.
The root غدر (gdr) primarily means to act perfidiously, unfaithfully, or treacherously, breaking a compact or neglecting its fulfillment. It is the opposite of faithfulness.
The root عضد (EDd) primarily refers to the upper arm, from the elbow to the shoulder. Figuratively, it signifies an "aider," "assistant," or "support," and can also denote "strength.
The root وبق (wbq) primarily signifies perishing, being destroyed, or falling into ruin. It also conveys the idea of being bound or held back, leading to destruction.
The root Hqb primarily refers to something carried behind, like a saddlebag for provisions. It can also metaphorically describe a burden one carries or lays up for the future.
The root غطو (gTw) primarily means to cover or conceal something, or to come upon or over it.
The word "manjaniq" refers to a siege engine, similar to the Roman Onager or balista. It was used to hurl projectiles.
The root أرب (Arb) conveys meanings of cunning, intelligence, and skill, as well as being accustomed to something.
The root ضمم primarily signifies joining things together, adding one thing to another, or including something within a larger whole. It conveys the idea of combining or incorporating elements.
The root أزر (azr) primarily refers to a waist-wrapper, a non-sewn garment covering the lower body. Metaphorically, it signifies preparation, chastity, or one's wife/family.
The root قوع (qwE) refers to a level, plain, or soft piece of land. It is often described as low-lying, free from mountains, and sometimes as land that produces nothing.
The root هضم (hDm) primarily refers to something melting or dissolving after being congealed. It also describes fruit becoming broken, crushed, or mellow, making it easy to digest.
The root خمد (khmd) describes fire subsiding, its flames dying down while embers remain. It also applies to fever abating or a sick person fainting or dying.

The root خردل (khrdl) refers to mustard seed, a well-known grain with various medicinal properties. It is described as heating, emollient, and beneficial for ailments like gout, sciatica, and leprosy.
The root نفش (nfsh) primarily means to separate or loosen something with fingers, like cotton or wool.
The root غوص (gwS) primarily means to dive into water, often to retrieve something like pearls. Tropically, it extends to deeply understanding or eliciting hidden meanings, like diving for knowledge.
A مُضْغَةٌ (muḍghah) is a piece or bit of flesh, like a morsel one chews. It can also refer to a fetus in its early stage, resembling a lump of flesh, as mentioned in the Quran (22:5).
The root صهر (ṣiḥr) primarily denotes relationship by marriage, like in-laws.
The root عتق (Etq) conveys meanings of excellence, nobility, and antiquity. It describes something that is swift, excellent, or choice, like a noble horse or a superior hawk.
The root سحق (sHq) primarily means to bruise, bray, or pound something, often finely, or to wear something out. It can also describe wind effacing traces on the ground or time wearing out a garment.
The root عرر (ʿ-r-r) primarily refers to a disease affecting camels, causing their bodies to become covered in sores or scabs.
The root عطل (ETl) primarily describes a woman without ornaments. It extends to being destitute of anything, like property or discipline.
The root غثو relates to accumulation and unpleasantness. It describes a valley filled with debris, lean meat, or a nauseous feeling.
The root نكب (nkb) primarily describes deviation or turning away from a straight path.
The root عبث (Ebth) primarily means to mix or mingle. It also describes playing, sporting, or engaging in unprofitable actions.
The root وَدْقٌ (wdq) refers to rain, which can be either gentle or violent. Some sources specifically define it as violent rain.
The root هبو (hbw) describes ashes becoming mixed with dust and extinguishing. It also refers to embers dying out.
The root رتل (rtl) originally describes well-arranged, separate teeth. It evolved to mean arranging speech clearly and distinctly, often in a leisurely manner.
The root رَسَسَ (rassasa) primarily means to lay a foundation or to originate something.
The root مِلْحٌ primarily refers to salt, a well-known substance used to flavor food. It can also describe salt water.
The root خضع (khDE) primarily means to be lowly, humble, or submissive, often in body. It can also describe a soft manner of speech, especially between a man and a woman.
The root Q-L-Y primarily means to fry or roast something in a pan. It can also refer to hating or disliking someone intensely, as if burning them with your dislike.
The root هيم (hym) describes being bewildered or distracted by intense desire, often amorous.
The root سبأ (sbA) primarily relates to buying wine, specifically for drinking. It also describes fire or whips burning or altering skin, and figuratively, the sun or fever doing the same.
The root حجز (Hjz) primarily refers to the place where a garment is tied around the waist, like a belt or waistband. Figuratively, it denotes patience and hardiness, or abstaining from unlawful acts.
The root كبب primarily signifies overturning or throwing something down, especially on its face. It implies a forceful and complete inversion.
The root شطأ primarily refers to the shoot or sprout that emerges from a seed or plant, especially a grain. It signifies the initial growth or offshoot, like a young branch or sucker.
The root "srmd" signifies continuous, unending time, whether day or night. It describes something perpetual or everlasting, like an endless night.
The root خدد primarily refers to making a furrow or groove in the ground, like a track or a ditch. It can also describe a deep cut or mark on a surface, or a wrinkle on the skin.
The root سبغ (sbg) describes something complete, full, ample, or without deficiency, often implying length. It's used for a long coat of mail, a full tail, or a copious rain.
The root حنجر (Hnjr) is mentioned in dictionaries like the K as a quadriliteral root.
The root مزق (mzq) primarily means to tear or rend something severely, often in multiple places, leading to mangling or dismemberment.
The root لغب (lgb) primarily describes bad, disordered, or ill-composed feathers of an arrow, especially when they are uneven or incongruous.
The root شَغَلَ (shagala) means to busy, occupy, or divert someone. It often implies being distracted from one thing by another. The passive form شُغِلَ بِهِ means to be occupied by something.
The primary meaning of R-M-M relates to decay, crumbling, or becoming old and worn out.
The root ثقب (thqb) primarily means to make a small, penetrating hole, like boring pearls or piercing an ear.
The root "nzf" primarily means to exhaust something completely, like draining a well of its water. It implies a thorough depletion.
The root سقم (saqima) means to be diseased, sick, or ill. It can refer to physical sickness, but also metaphorically to a "diseased heart" or "unsound understanding.
The root نعج (nEj) primarily describes something being of a clear, pure white color.
The root "Hnth" primarily means to put away sin or crime, or to do works to escape it. It can also mean to apply oneself to devotion, abstain from sin, or relinquish idols.
The root QHM refers to something redundant, pleonastic, or foisted in. It's often used for words or letters inserted without reason, essentially meaning "superfluous" or "extra."
The root كَوَّرَ (kawwara) means to wind, wrap, or fold something, like a turban. It describes the sun being wrapped in darkness or losing its light, and God causing night to cover day.
The root "hyj" primarily means to become roused, excited, or stirred up, like dust or blood. It also describes a camel's lustful excitement or an eye becoming inflamed.
The root ZMR relates to making a sound, like playing a reed pipe or the cry of an ostrich. It can also mean to divulge a story or incite someone.
The root Azf signifies drawing near or hastening. It describes something, like a time or departure, becoming imminent. In the Quran, it refers to the Day of Resurrection drawing near.
The root دَخَنَ (dakhana) primarily refers to smoke rising from fire or other sources.
The root ق-ي-ض (q-y-ḍ) primarily means to cleave, break, or rent asunder, like an egg hatching or the sky splitting.
The root كَمَمَ primarily means to cover or conceal something, often by wrapping or enclosing it. It can refer to covering a pot, a sword in its sheath, or a woman's head.
The root غلي primarily means to boil or bubble up, like water or a pot.
The root عتل (Etl) refers to something strong and robust. It describes tools like a carpenter's auger, an iron implement for uprooting palm trees, or a large rod for demolishing walls.
The root دهر (dahr) primarily means "time," specifically a long, indefinite period, or even eternity. It can also refer to a shorter duration, or metaphorically, to fate or fortune.
The root عيي primarily signifies being unable, incapable, or powerless to do something. It also conveys the idea of being ignorant or unskilled in a matter, leading to failure or frustration.
The root ضغن (Dgn) primarily signifies rancor, malice, or intense hatred. It can also describe a difficult disposition in animals or an inclination/desire towards something or someone.
The term مَحُونَةٌ (maḥūnah) is defined by referring to the root حين (ḥīn).
The root شعب (sha'aba) refers to division or branching. It can describe a branch of a tree, a cleft in a mountain, or a small watercourse.
The root "sahw" primarily means to be unmindful, forgetful, or neglectful of something, often due to one's mind being elsewhere. It can imply a slight oversight rather than complete oblivion.
The root "mwr" describes movement, often side-to-side, to and fro, or in commotion. It can refer to physical objects swaying, dust rising, or even the heavens reeling.
The root دعع (daʿʿa) primarily means to push or repel with force, often with a shove or thrust. It implies a strong, sometimes violent, expulsion or driving away.
The root كَهَن (k-h-n) primarily refers to foretelling future events, often with a sense of mystery or hidden knowledge.
The root LMM primarily means to collect, gather, or bring together. It can also refer to approaching or drawing near.
The root أشر (Ashr) primarily means to saw wood. It also describes a woman filing her teeth to make them serrated.
The root جَلَل (jll) primarily signifies greatness, majesty, and importance. It can also refer to covering or encompassing something, like a garment or a large object.
The root شأم primarily refers to the left side or direction. It is associated with misfortune, ill-omen, or bad luck, as the left hand was traditionally considered inauspicious.
The root W-J-F primarily denotes movement, trembling, or throbbing, often with a sense of agitation or fear.
The root Q-T-F relates to gathering or plucking, especially fruits like grapes. It can refer to the act of harvesting or the time of harvest.
The root عهن (Ehn) primarily means remaining or continuing, but can also mean going forth, showing contradictory senses. It describes something present, ready, or long-possessed, like property.
The root لَبَدَ (labada) primarily means to stick or adhere, especially to the ground. It can describe a bird lying on its breast or a person staying fixed in a place.
The root خنس (khns) primarily means to go back, recede, or retreat, often implying hiding or shrinking.

The root بعثر (baʿthara) means to uncover, raise, or bring forth what is hidden, like treasures from graves. It also means to scatter, disperse, or turn things over, and to examine or search for news.

The root LFW (تَلَافَى) means to repair or set right something that is deficient or inconsistent. It implies correcting a shortcoming or making amends.
The root دلو (dalw) primarily means to let down a bucket into a well to draw water.

The root عزر (ʿazara) means to discipline, punish, or chastise someone to deter them from wrongdoing. It can also mean to aid, strengthen, or treat with reverence.

The root "Sdf" primarily refers to anything high or lofty, like a wall or mountain. It also denotes the side of a mountain or the space between two mountains.
The root أفل (Afl) refers to a young camel, typically in its second or third year, or a young weaned camel.
The root رمن (rmn) primarily refers to the pomegranate fruit (رُمَّانٌ). It can also denote the white poppy or a species of hypericum.

The root طَلَبَ (ṭalaba) primarily means to seek, desire, demand, or ask for something. It can also imply pursuing or following in search of something.
The root لقف (lqf) means to seize or take something quickly, especially if it's thrown or said to you. It implies a swift and immediate grasp.
The root سَلَخَ (salakha) primarily means to strip off a skin, like from an animal. It extends metaphorically to stripping off clothes, or the passing of time, like a month ending.
The root مَتْن (matn) primarily refers to the strong, firm parts of the back, specifically the erector spinae muscles or the two fleshy portions flanking the backbone.
The root HFW primarily describes walking barefoot or having worn-down feet. It also conveys showing great honor, kindness, and diligent inquiry towards someone.
The root نفل (nafal) refers to something extra or exceeding the original. It can mean a voluntary gift, alms, or a good deed beyond what is obligatory.
The root ردف (rdf) primarily means to ride behind someone or something, or to follow closely. It can also describe an event happening unexpectedly or suddenly.
The root R-K-M signifies things being heaped, piled up, or accumulated, one part upon another.
The root سَيْح (sayḥ) describes something becoming large, wide, or unstraitened, like a belly or a state of mind.
The root "ljA" means to seek refuge or shelter. The eighth form, "iltajā," carries the same meaning, emphasizing the act of resorting to someone or something for protection.
The root ظمأ primarily signifies thirst, a strong desire for water. It can also denote a state of being thirsty or parched, both literally and metaphorically, implying a deep need or longing.

The root "rhT" refers to a small group of men, typically 3 to 10, excluding women, often one's close kinsfolk. It can also mean an enemy.
The root ت ب ب primarily signifies perishing, being ruined, or suffering loss. It implies a state of destruction, failure, or being cut off from good.
The root زفر relates to bearing burdens. It describes a bulky camel, the withers of an animal, or the foundational corner of a building.
The primary meaning of ذأب (dhAb) refers to the wolf, known for its predatory nature and cunning.
The root صبو (Sbw) primarily means to be youthful, ignorant, or foolish, often implying amorous dalliance. It also signifies inclining the heart towards someone or something, yearning, or longing.
A "ضِغْث" (dgith) is a handful of mixed herbs or twigs. It can also refer to anything collected together, like a bundle.
The root حوج (Hwj) primarily signifies "want," "need," or "necessity." It also refers to "a thing wanted" or "an object of need.
The root عير (Eyr) primarily refers to an ass, both wild and domestic, known for wandering. It also denotes a lord or chief.
The root فَقَدَ (faqada) means to lose, miss, or not find something. It implies absence from perception, where the item's location is unknown.
The root برح (brH) primarily signifies 'to depart' or 'to cease.' It can describe physical departure from a place or the cessation of a state, like a secret becoming apparent.
The root شكو (shkw) primarily means to complain or show grief. It can refer to complaining about a person, a situation, or an illness.
The root زجو (zjw) primarily means to push or drive gently, to urge something on. It can refer to making days pass, driving camels, or the wind driving clouds.
The root سيل (syl) primarily refers to the "tongue" or tang of a sword or knife, the part that extends into the handle.
The root مَحَا (maḥā) means to efface, erase, or obliterate something, removing its trace or impression.
The root س و غ relates to ease of swallowing. It describes making something easy to swallow, like a drink, or swallowing something easily oneself.
The root هطع (hTE) primarily describes a state of being humbled, submissive, or looking down in fear or shame.
The root زول (zwl) primarily means to go away, pass away, or depart. It describes something ceasing to exist, removing from its place, or the sun declining from the meridian.
The root جأر (jAr) primarily signifies raising the voice in supplication or complaint, often with a sense of distress or urgency.
The root عجم (ʿajama) primarily means to bite or chew, especially to test hardness.
The root "Aff" primarily denotes a sound or expression of disgust, impatience, or contempt, often made by blowing or exhaling. It signifies a strong dislike or disapproval, as in saying "Uff!
The root مرح (marah) primarily describes excessive joy, exultation, and pride, often leading to insolent or ungrateful behavior.
The root ستر (str) primarily means to veil, conceal, or cover something, providing protection or shelter. It can refer to a veil, curtain, or screen.
The root فزز (fzz) primarily means to startle, to be startled, or to flee in alarm.
The root رقي primarily signifies ascending, rising, or going upwards, whether physically or in status.
The root LFF primarily means to wrap, fold, or roll something up, often implying a close or tight enclosure. It can also refer to things that are intertwined or dense, like thick foliage.
The Arabic word "dihqan" is borrowed from Persian, meaning "headman of a village." It refers to a chief, proprietor, or a wealthy landowner, especially in Persia.
The root خفت (khft) primarily describes a voice becoming still, silent, low, or weak. It extends to mean ceasing to speak, dying, or dying suddenly.
The root رَقَمَ (rqm) primarily means "to write" or "to seal/stamp." It also refers to marking or decorating cloth, often with stripes or figures.
The root شطط primarily means to exceed the just limit, to deviate from the right course, or to act excessively and unjustly.
The root وَصِيدٌ (waṣīd) primarily refers to an open space or court in front of a house, a threshold, or a door. It can also denote a stone enclosure for livestock in the mountains.
The root صخر (ṣakhr) refers to rocks or large, hard masses of stone. The singular form is صخرة (ṣakhrah).
The root "sfn" describes the act of stripping, scraping, or paring off an outer layer, like wind removing dust from the ground. It also refers to smoothing something or a ship sticking to the ground.
The root شيب (shyb) primarily describes something white-haired or hoary, like an old person. It can also be used metaphorically for mountains white with snow or frost, or even white truffles.
A "jadh'a" refers to a young animal, typically before its prime, with specific age definitions varying by species (e.g., a year-old sheep, a two-year-old bull, a five-year-old camel).
The root جثو (jthw) primarily refers to collected stones or earth, forming a mound or hillock, often associated with graves. It can also denote a live coal or the middle part of something.
The root قبس (qbs) primarily means to take or acquire fire from a source. This concept extends metaphorically to acquiring knowledge or catching a fever from someone else.
The root نَسَفَ (nasafa) primarily describes the action of wind carrying something away, like dust. It implies scattering or dispersing something lightly, similar to how wind blows things away.
The root عري primarily means to be or become naked, bare, or unclothed. It can also refer to being devoid of something, like a place being bare of vegetation or a person being without possessions.
The root ركض (rkD) primarily means to strike or move with the leg or foot, often to urge something. It can also describe running, fleeing, or a bird moving its wings.
The root فجج (fajj) primarily describes a wide opening or space, like a broad road or a valley. It implies something being split open or having a large, expansive gap.
The root نكس (nks) primarily means to turn something over, invert it, or reverse its state. It can describe turning something upside down or making the first part last.
The root بهج (bhj) describes something beautiful, goodly, or bright, especially plants. It also refers to a person being joyful, glad, or happy, often with a radiant appearance.
The root W-TH-N refers to an idol, similar to other terms like S-N-M, '-TH-N, and '-N-N. It denotes an object of worship other than God.
The root S-L-L primarily means to draw out or extract something smoothly and gently, like pulling a sword from its scabbard or hair from dough.
The root "wtr" primarily means to make something odd or singular, like making a number odd or performing a prayer with an odd number of units.
The root "hmz" means to press, squeeze, or pinch something. It also signifies pushing, striking, or goading. Figuratively, it refers to the devil's evil suggestions or blaming/reproaching someone.
Barzakh refers to an intervening barrier or obstruction between two things. In a religious context, it denotes the period between death and resurrection.
The root "nsb" primarily means to mention or trace one's lineage or genealogy. It also extends to attributing or ascribing something to someone or something else.
The root جيب (jyb) primarily refers to the opening of a garment at the neck or bosom, like a shirt's collar.
The root "nthr" primarily means to scatter, sprinkle, or strew something. It can also refer to a palm tree shedding unripe dates or a person having many children.
The root فُرَاتٌ (furāt) primarily describes water that is very sweet and quenches thirst. It is also the name of the Euphrates River, a major river flowing through Iraq.
The root أجج (Ajj) primarily describes the act of kindling or setting something ablaze, causing it to burn fiercely.
The root شحن (shHn) primarily means to fill, like filling a ship or a city with horsemen. It also means to drive away or remove someone or something.
The root صرح (SrH) signifies clarity and manifestation. It describes a camel yielding pure milk, wine becoming clear, or a day free of clouds.
The root Hdq primarily refers to the black part of the eye, including the iris and pupil. It can also denote the entire eye.
The root جدث (jdth) refers to a grave or sepulchre. The plural forms are أَجْدَاثٌ and أَجْدُثٌ.
The root لذذ primarily means to be sweet, delicious, or pleasant. It refers to something that is agreeable to the taste or senses, causing enjoyment and delight.
The root "zqm" primarily refers to "zaqqum," a tree in Hell with repulsive fruit, described as a deadly, bitter food.
The root "rwg" primarily means to turn aside or away, often with deceit or guile, like a fox. It implies quick, evasive movement, or secretly returning or turning towards something.
A *watid* is a wooden peg, pin, or stake fixed in the ground or a wall. It can also metaphorically refer to mountains (pegs of the earth), chiefs of lands, or teeth.
The root س ل س ل (slsl) primarily describes something that is smooth, easy, or flowing. It can refer to water that is easy to swallow or a chain that is smooth and flexible.
The root سجر primarily means to fill something, often with water, or to heat an oven by filling it with fuel. It can also describe a camel's prolonged cry or making hair hang down.
The root صرصر (SrSr) primarily describes a strong, loud, and piercing sound, often associated with wind. It conveys the idea of a violent, shrieking noise, like a whirlwind or a powerful gust.
The root نَحْس (nHs) describes something unprosperous, unfortunate, or inauspicious. It can refer to a person, a day, or even a year of drought.
The root أفق (Afq) primarily means to go one's own way, often into distant regions. It also signifies reaching the utmost degree in generosity, knowledge, or eloquence, as if reaching the horizon.
The root ثلل (thll) primarily means to be broken, to fall down, or to be humbled. It can refer to the breaking of a thing, like a wall, or the breaking of one's power or glory, leading to abasement.
The root "Tbq" primarily means a thing that is the equal of another, like a lid covering its container.
The root صرم (Srm) primarily means to cut or sever something, like a rope or fruit from a tree. It also extends to metaphorically cutting off a relationship or friendship.
The root HDD primarily means to incite, urge, or encourage someone to do something, often with a sense of hastening or pressing them. It implies a strong motivation or instigation towards an action.
The root عبس (Ebs) primarily means to frown, contract one's face, or look sternly. It can also describe a day that is distressful or calamitous.
The root مزج (mzj) refers to mixing or mingling. It can describe an admixture, what is mixed with a drink, or the constitution/temperament of the body (its humors).
The root لهب (lhb) primarily describes fire flaming or blazing, especially without smoke. It also refers to lightning flashing continuously.
The root زلل primarily means to slip, stumble, or err, often unintentionally. It implies a loss of footing or stability, leading to a fall or deviation from the right path.
The root خَسَأَ primarily means to drive away, repel, or cast out with contempt and disgrace. It implies being rejected and sent back in a state of humiliation, often like a dog being driven away.
The root قفو (qafaw) primarily means to follow someone's tracks or footsteps, to track them. It implies following closely behind, similar to tracing their path.
The root خَصَص primarily means to be unique, distinct, or particular to something.
The root نسخ (nskh) means to annul, supersede, or replace something with another, like the sun replacing shade. It also means to change, alter, or transform something, or to copy/transcribe a text.
The root HSD primarily means to envy someone for a blessing, wishing it would depart from them.
The root H-A-T primarily means to come, bring, or fetch. It often implies bringing something forth or causing it to appear.
The root بدع (bdE) primarily means to originate or invent something new, without a pre-existing model.
The root خ ط و (kha-ṭa-wa) means to step or walk over something or someone. It implies passing beyond or transgressing a boundary.
The root طوق (Twq) primarily refers to an arch or curved structure, often in buildings. It can also denote a layer or single piece of something, like a sole of a shoe or a single-ply garment.

The root شور (shwr) primarily means to gather honey. It also signifies exhibiting or displaying something, especially an animal for sale, often involving testing its capabilities.
The root نشز (nshz) primarily means to rise or elevate oneself. It can describe rising in a place, or a physical object being high or prominent.

Amd (أمد) refers to a period of time with a defined end, or the utmost limit of something. It can denote the span of one's life, or the start and end points in a race.
The root QLM refers to a writing reed or pen. It is used for writing, similar to the meaning of the root JLM.
The term هِيْئَةٌ (hay'ah) refers to the form, shape, or appearance of something. It can also denote the state, condition, or manner in which something exists or is done.
The root فشل (fashala) primarily means to be cowardly, weak, or flagging. It describes a state of timidity or lack of resolve.
The root فَوْر (fawr) primarily describes boiling or effervescence, like water boiling or anger flaring up. It also refers to things gushing forth, such as water from the earth or blood from a vein.

The root سَجْلٌ (sajl) primarily refers to a full bucket of water, or a great bucket.

The root صرخ (Srkh) means to cry out or scream, often vehemently, due to fright, alarm, or affliction. It also signifies calling for aid or succour.
The root SlSl primarily describes the sound of dry clay or pottery when struck, a clinking or ringing sound. It also refers to the sound of a bridle or chain, and by extension, the sound of a bell.
The root HMA relates to black, fetid mud. It describes cleaning a well of this mud, or water/wells becoming turbid and foul-smelling due to it. It can also mean to be angry with someone.
The root سقف (sqf) primarily refers to a roof or covering, like a porch or a plank used for roofing.
The root دخر (dkhr) describes being object, mean, contemptible, or despicable. It implies a state of lowliness or abasement.
The root عتب (Etb) primarily means to be angry with someone, especially with the anger of a friend, or to reprove/blame them.
The root نَفَدَ (nfd) primarily means to come to an end, be exhausted, or consumed. It can describe provisions running out, property being spent, or a well losing its water.
The root غسق (gsq) primarily describes darkness, especially the intense darkness of night. It also refers to eyes shedding tears or overflowing, and wounds discharging yellow fluid.
The root "thabr" means to confine, restrain, or prevent someone from something. It also means to deny, refuse, or disappoint someone.
The root دحض (dHD) primarily means to slip, like a foot or the sun declining. It also metaphorically describes an argument becoming null or void, as if it slipped away from validity.
The root طوي primarily means to fold, roll up, or coil. It also conveys the idea of traversing or passing over a distance, as if folding it up.
The root سمر (smr) primarily means to converse or stay awake at night. It also describes cattle pasturing at night or drinking wine at night.
The root طفل (Tfl) primarily refers to a young one, infant, or child, from birth until puberty. It can also denote a portion of something, like a spark of fire or small clouds.

The root صبب (Sbb) primarily means to pour out or shed liquid, often in a continuous or abundant manner. It can also refer to something falling or descending rapidly, like rain or water from a height.
The root عقم (Eqm) primarily describes barrenness, like a womb unable to conceive or a person unable to have children.
The root دَهَنَ (dhn) primarily means to anoint or oil something, like hair or skin. It can also describe rain lightly moistening the earth.
The root "ljj" primarily describes something that is deep, vast, or enters deeply into something else.
The root غضض (gDD) primarily means to lower, diminish, or restrain something, often referring to the gaze or voice. It implies a sense of modesty, humility, or reduction.
The root "srj" primarily means to lie or forge a lie. It can also describe something being bright or a face becoming beautiful. Additionally, it refers to a woman plaiting her hair.
The root "mhn" refers to work, labor, or service, including the performance of an office or ministration. It can also denote the clothes worn while performing such duties.
سِدْر (sidr) refers to the lote-tree, specifically *Rhamnus spina Christi* or *Rhamnus nabeca*. Its fruit is called nabq. The leaves are used for ritual washing.
The root كُوبَةٌ (kūbah) refers to games like backgammon (نَرْد) or chess (شِطْرَنْج), especially in Yemen. It can also mean a small, slender drum or a musical instrument called بَرْبَط.
The root عثو (ʿathaw) primarily means to act corruptly or make mischief, often to an extreme degree. It can also refer to acting wrongfully or unjustly.
The root مصر (m-ṣ-r) refers to a partition, barrier, or limit between two things, like a boundary between lands.
The root نكل (nkl) refers to a punishment that serves as a deterrent. It warns others not to commit similar offenses and restrains the offender from repeating the crime.
The root Sfr relates to emptiness, hunger, and a yellowing disease. It also refers to a serpent believed to cause hunger pangs.
The root ثور (thwr) primarily means to be raised, roused, excited, or stirred up, like dust or smoke.
Lane's Lexicon indicates that the term "درّيء" (darri'un) and its variations are cross-referenced to a subsequent entry for their definition. This means the meaning is found elsewhere in the lexicon.
The root حرص (HrS) primarily means to tear, cleave, or strip off a surface. It also signifies an intense, often greedy or culpable, desire for something, or striving diligently to attain it.
The root سبط (sbT) primarily describes something lank or straight, especially hair, as opposed to curly. It can also refer to a person who is tall, well-proportioned, or has long fingers.
The root "wsT" primarily refers to the middle part of something, often implying equal distance from extremes, like the center of a circle.
The root جوع (jwE) primarily signifies hunger or emptiness of the belly, the opposite of fullness. It can also refer to a year of famine.
The root خنزر (khnzr) is directly linked to the root خزر (khzr). To understand its meaning, one should refer to the definitions provided under the root خزر.
The root H-L-L primarily signifies appearing, shining, or becoming visible, like the new moon. It also conveys the idea of beginning something, especially a new month.
The root أدي (Ady) primarily means to perform, execute, or fulfill a duty, trust, or promise. It also conveys the sense of paying or rendering something due.
The root كمل (kml) primarily means to be or become perfect. It can also mean complete, entire, whole, or full, though the root تمم (tmm) is more precise for these latter meanings.
The root عنت (Ent) primarily describes falling into difficulty or hardship. It can also refer to a bone breaking after healing, or a beast becoming lame.
The root بعل (ba'l) primarily refers to a husband, lord, or owner. It can also denote an idol worshipped by ancient peoples, as mentioned in the Quran.
The root "srH" primarily describes cattle grazing freely, especially in the morning. It extends to actions of sending forth or releasing, like sending a messenger or a torrent flowing easily.

The root قتر (qtr) relates to emitting a scent, like roast meat or smoke.
The root غرف (grf) primarily refers to a type of tree used for tanning hides and making bows.
The root "jwz" often relates to passing or making something pass. It can mean to allow, permit, or make something lawful, like a contract or an opinion.
The root خوي primarily signifies emptiness, hollowness, or being void.
The root 'ESr' primarily means to press or squeeze something to extract its contents, like juice from grapes or water from a cloth.
The root LWY primarily signifies bending, twisting, or turning something. It can also denote evading, delaying, or distorting.
The root نَقَذ (nqdh) refers to something saved, rescued, or liberated, like a person or a horse taken from an enemy. It can also denote a coat of mail, as it saves the wearer.
The root بغض (bgD) primarily means to hate. The verb أَبْغَضَ (abghaḍa) signifies "he hated him.
The root خيب (khyb) signifies failure or disappointment. It describes an attempt that doesn't yield the desired result, like a fire-starter that fails to ignite.
The root رعب (rEb) primarily means to fear, be afraid, or be terrified, often to the utmost degree, filling one's heart with dread. It can also mean to cause fear or to threaten.
The root فوت (fwt) primarily conveys the idea of something passing or escaping.
The root "lyn" describes something that is soft, gentle, or pliable. It can refer to physical softness, a smooth surface, or a gentle disposition.
The root "rbT" primarily means to tie or bind. It refers to horses kept tied, often for military readiness. The term also describes a monk or sage who restrains themselves from worldly pleasures.
The root سدد (sadd) primarily means to be or make straight, right, or direct. It also conveys the idea of hitting the mark, being accurate, or being guided to the right way.
The root مقت (mqt) signifies intense hatred, often due to a foul deed. It describes being an object of extreme dislike or detestation.
The root لمس (lms) primarily means to feel or touch, often with the hand, to test or perceive. It can also tropically mean to have sexual intercourse or to kiss.
The root طمس (Tms) primarily means to efface or obliterate something, like a trace or writing. It can also describe a star or eye losing its light, or a heart becoming corrupt.
The root رفق (rfq) signifies gentleness, kindness, and acting with ease. It describes being gentle with others, performing tasks skillfully, or proceeding moderately.
The root "mrd" primarily describes softening or mashing something, like bread in water. It also refers to a youth being beardless or a tree being leafless, implying a lack of something.
The root "HyS" is primarily found in the idiom "ḥayṣa bayṣa," meaning to fall into confusion, straitness, or difficulty from which there is no escape.
The root صيد (Syd) primarily means to hunt, capture, or ensnare game, fish, or fowl. It can also be used metaphorically to mean captivating people with kindness or obtaining what one desires.
The root شرع (shar'a) primarily means to enter water to drink, or to begin an action. It also signifies making something clear or apparent, like a road or a law.
The root حمي (Hmy) primarily means to protect, guard, or defend something or someone from harm or danger.
The root "myd" primarily describes motion, agitation, or swaying, like the earth shaking or a branch bending. It also refers to a feeling of giddiness or nausea.
The root بلس (bls) refers to the balsam tree, specifically the species producing the balsam of Mecca. This tree, or shrub, has fragrant leaves and berries.
A *ṣanam* is an idol, often a carved image of wood, metal, or stone, typically in human form, that is worshipped. It is distinguished from a *wathan*, which can be shapeless or of other forms.
The root كوكب (kwkb) refers to a star or planet. It is related to the root ككب (kkb), which also denotes celestial bodies. The term encompasses both individual stars and planets.
The root فَرْدَ (fard) signifies being single, sole, or alone, without equal or companion. It describes something unique, individual, or separate from others.
The root خَرص (khrS) primarily means to estimate or conjecture, especially regarding palm fruit. This can extend to any speech based on opinion rather than certainty.
The root "shrH" means to uncover, open, or explain something, making it clear. It can also mean to cut meat or to understand speech.
The root وسوس (wsws) primarily means to whisper, suggest evil, or tempt. It describes the act of secretly instigating bad thoughts or actions, often associated with the devil's influence.
The root جثم (jthm) primarily refers to the body or person, similar to جِسْمٌ or شَخْصٌ. It can describe the physical form of a human or even an animal.
The root جَلَا (jlw) primarily means to be clear, apparent, or manifest. It also describes going forth or emigrating from a place, often due to fear or drought.
The root "Asf" describes intense grief, lamenting, or regret, often due to loss. It also conveys being easily saddened and tender-hearted.
The root Hwt relates to striving or enticing someone to turn from something, often with guile, like a fish in water.
The root W-J-L primarily signifies being afraid or terrified, often with a trembling or shaking component. It describes a state of fear that causes physical agitation or a deep sense of dread.
The root مضي primarily signifies passing, going forth, or proceeding. It can refer to time passing, or a person or thing moving onward and away.
The root قَصْو (qaṣw) primarily refers to being distant or far away, both physically and metaphorically.
The root ذمم primarily signifies blame, censure, or dispraise.
The root وطأ (w-T-ʾ) primarily means "to tread upon" or "to trample." It can also refer to making something plain or soft, or to a place being easy to traverse.
The root لزم (lzm) means to necessitate, oblige, or make something cleave to someone. It implies a strong, often inescapable, connection or decree.
The root عَصَبَ primarily means to twist, wind, fold, or bind something tightly. It can refer to binding a ram's testicles or a she-camel's thighs.
The root Q-D-D primarily means to cut or slit something lengthwise, often referring to tearing or splitting.
The root قرع (qrE) primarily means to strike or hit. It can refer to striking with a stick or sword, or even filliping with fingers.
The root "bwr" primarily means to perish or become corrupt. It describes land becoming barren, work being in vain, or goods becoming unsaleable.

The root قطر primarily means to drip or fall in drops, like water or tears. It can also describe arranging camels in a file or string. Figuratively, it can mean to go away quickly or to sew a garment.
The root شهب (shhb) primarily describes a color: a mix of white and black, often a grayish hue.
The root صدع (SdE) primarily means to cleave, split, or crack something, like a wall or glass. It extends to traversing a desert or journeying through the night.
The root ZNY primarily refers to unlawful sexual intercourse, specifically fornication or adultery. It encompasses the act itself and the state of being an adulterer/fornicator.
The root صَوْت (ṣawt) refers to a sound, noise, voice, or cry, applicable to humans and other things. It can also mean a clamor or a cry for help.
The root HSB primarily means to pelt with pebbles or to spread pebbles. It also refers to throwing things into a fire or kindling a fire.
The term "كاسف البال" (kāsif al-bāl) is defined by referring to the entry for "بال" (bāl). This suggests that its meaning is closely tied to or explained within the definition of "bāl" itself.
The root "mhl" (أمهل) means to act gently or leisurely towards someone, granting them delay or respite. It implies giving someone time to do something, like saying, "Give me time to do such a thing."
The root أرك (Ark) primarily describes camels feeding on Arak trees or remaining in a place. Tropically, it refers to a person staying put, persisting in an affair, or even holding back.
The root H-Z-Z primarily means to shake or be shaken, often with force or repetition. It can describe the shaking of a spear, a tree, or even a person.
The root شتت primarily means to scatter, disperse, or separate things widely. It implies a state of disunity and fragmentation, often referring to people or affairs being broken up and spread apart.
The root "برد" primarily means to be or become cold, chill, or cool, often implying a cessation of heat or motion. It can metaphorically refer to death, stillness, or the allaying of pain.
The root وزع (wazʿa) refers to a group of people, like assistants or followers. It can also describe someone who restrains or prevents.
The root فَوْجٌ (fawj) refers to a company, group, or party of people, often a dense crowd or multitude. It can also denote followers or dependants of leaders.
The root زجر (zjr) primarily means to chide, check, or restrain someone with a cry or rough speech. It also describes driving animals with a specific cry, like camels or sheep.
The root ضوأ (DwA) in form V, تضوّأ, describes someone standing in darkness to observe others by the light of their fire, without being seen themselves.
The root بكم (bkm) describes someone who is dumb, either by birth or unable to articulate words well, even if they can speak. It can also refer to someone lacking understanding or intellect.

The root خَطَفَ (khaṭafa) means to seize, snatch, or carry off by force or quickly. It can describe a sword striking off a head, lightning taking away sight, or a devil stealing a hearing opportunity.
The root فرش (frsh) primarily means to spread or expand something, like spreading a bed or a carpet. It can also metaphorically mean to make an affair ample or to lay oneself open for others.
The root نَدَدَ (ndd) primarily means to flee or run away, often in fear or aversion. It can also imply being equal or a match for something, or to be a rival.
The root قسو primarily means to be hard, severe, or unyielding. It describes something that is tough and not easily affected or softened, like a stone.
The root أسر (Asr) primarily means to bind or capture, like tying a saddle or taking a prisoner. It can also refer to God's perfect creation of something.
The root نسك (nsk) primarily means to devote oneself to religious exercises or devotion. It describes someone who becomes a devout worshipper, engaging in acts of piety.
The root كرر (krr) primarily signifies repetition, reiteration, or doing something again. It implies a return to a previous state or action, often with the sense of turning back or circling.
The root ثقف (thqf) means to become skilled, intelligent, or quick. It also refers to perceiving or attaining something quickly, often implying finding, overcoming, or taking hold of it.
The root H-S-R generally means to confine, restrict, or prevent. It can describe being surrounded by an enemy, detained from travel (especially pilgrimage), or suffering from physical constipation.
The root خلط (khlT) primarily means to mix or mingle. It can refer to physical mixing, like water with milk, or more abstract concepts like a disease infecting someone or anxiety pervading the heart.
The root فَآءَ (fyA) primarily means "to return," often implying a return to a good state, obedience, or reconsideration.
The root فرغ primarily means to be empty or vacant. It extends to being free from work, finishing a task, or even dying (as the body becomes empty of the soul).
The root حمر (Hmr) primarily denotes the color red, but its meaning extends significantly.
The root دأب (daʾab) refers to a subterranean structure, often for cooling, like a cellar or vault. It's an arabicized word from Persian, meaning "cold water." The plural is sarādīb.
The root HSS primarily conveys the idea of perceiving or sensing something, often subtly. It can refer to feeling with the senses, hearing a sound, or having a premonition.
The root درس (drs) primarily means for something to become effaced, erased, or worn out, like traces, houses, or garments.
The root HBL primarily means "rope" or "cord," used for tying or as a halter. Metaphorically, it signifies a "bond," "connection," or "covenant," especially with God or people.
The root صرر (Srr) primarily means to tie or bind tightly, to gather or collect something into a bundle or purse, and to make a sound like a creak or chirp.
The root كظم (kzhm) primarily means to repress or restrain, especially one's wrath or rage. It implies holding back or suppressing something, often an emotion.
The root لحق (lHq) primarily means to reach, overtake, or catch up with someone or something. It can also describe something becoming adjoined or annexed, or grief befalling someone.
The root خول (khwl) primarily refers to a maternal uncle or aunt. It also describes an owner or manager, especially of livestock, implying good care and management.
The root فخر (fkhr) primarily means to glory, boast, or praise oneself, often by recounting noble deeds or ancestry. It can also imply contending for superiority or disdaining others.
The root "skr" primarily means to be intoxicated or drunk. It also describes being violently angry or a watering trough becoming full.
The root "brj" refers to a tower, fortress, or a prominent part of a building. It can also denote the constellations or signs of the Zodiac in the heavens.
The root عَلِقَ (ʿaliqa) primarily means to hang, cling, or stick to something. It can also describe becoming attached by love, getting caught in a snare, or setting about an action.
The root ردي primarily signifies falling, perishing, or being destroyed. It can also mean to be clothed or to put on a garment, especially an upper garment.
The root Hbr refers to the "hubara," a type of bustard bird. It's known for its dust-colored plumage, long neck, and is often preyed upon.
The root قَصَدَ (qasada) primarily means to aim for, intend, or direct oneself towards something. It also conveys the sense of moderation, pursuing a right course, or acting justly.
The root "zyt" refers to the olive tree and its fruit. It's a well-known tree from which olive oil is extracted.
The root ذرأ primarily means to create, originate, or produce something from nothing, often referring to God's act of bringing forth creation.
The root نكث (nkth) primarily means to undo or untwist, like a rope. Tropically, it refers to breaking a promise or covenant, or a difficult affair that causes people to break agreements.
The root (lwH) primarily conveys the meaning of appearing, shining, or gleaming, like a star or lightning. It also describes something becoming apparent or manifest.
The root لحد (lHd) primarily means to decline, deviate, or incline.
The root رصد (rSd) refers to lying in wait or watching, often for an enemy, or a place for such. It can also mean a road or way.
The root شفي primarily means to heal or recover from illness. It also conveys the idea of being satisfied or having enough of something, like quenching thirst.
The root غرم (grm) primarily means to pay or discharge an obligation, like a debt or bloodwit.
The root عصف (ESf) primarily describes the violent blowing of wind. It also extends to express swiftness in movement, like a fast camel or horse.
The root "mwj" primarily describes the tumultuous, agitated motion of the sea and its waves.
The root ضيف (Dyf) primarily relates to inclining, leaning, or adjoining. It also signifies making someone a guest or offering refuge.
The root قمص (qmS) describes a horse or similar animal raising its forelegs and beating the ground with its hind legs, often when startled or restless.
The root بضع (bDE) refers to a small, indefinite number, typically from three to nine. It can also denote a number between thirteen and nineteen when combined with 'ashara (ten).
The root قنط (qnT) primarily means to despair, especially of God's mercy or of good. It can also imply a most vehement form of despair. In some contexts, it means to withhold or debar something.
The root تسع (tisʿ) refers to the number nine. It can be masculine (تِسْعَةٌ) or feminine (تِسْعٌ) depending on the noun it modifies.
The primary meaning of كهف (khf) refers to a cave or cavern, a large hollow in a mountain.
The root "zwr" primarily means to honor a visitor. However, it also encompasses meanings of falsifying, embellishing, or rectifying speech or testimony.
The root فزع (fazaʿa) primarily means to fear or be frightened. It can also mean to seek or give aid, often in response to fear or distress.
The root لؤلؤ primarily refers to pearls, specifically large, round, and lustrous ones. It denotes precious gems found in shells, valued for their beauty and rarity.
The root مَرَجَ (maraja) primarily means to send animals to pasture freely. It also signifies mixing things, like two seas that meet but don't fully blend.
The root حطم (HTm) primarily means to break, especially something dry or tough, like a bone. It can also mean to crush or bruise, as a lion crushes its prey or people in a crowd.
The primary meaning of كأس (kās) is a "cup" or "goblet" from which one drinks. It specifically refers to a vessel that contains liquid, often wine, and is ready for drinking.
The root عمه (Emh) describes being confounded, perplexed, and unable to find the right path, often wandering in error. It refers to mental confusion, unlike عَمَى (Amā), which is physical blindness.
The root بَرَقَ (brq) primarily means to shine or gleam, like lightning or a polished sword. It also describes threatening, or a woman beautifying herself.
The root "sbt" primarily means to rest, cease from work, or be still. It's famously used for the Jewish Sabbath, meaning to observe its ordinances or enter upon it.
The root LWN relates to color. It means to become colored, variegated, or diversified in color.
The root صَفْح (SfH) primarily refers to the side or lateral part of something, like the side of a face or a sword's flat.
The root خمر (khmr) primarily means to veil, cover, or conceal something. It extends to concealing thoughts, testimony, or even the intellect by wine.
The root عقد (Eqd) primarily means to tie or knot something firmly, like a rope. It extends to making contracts, oaths, or firm decisions.
The root نَصَفَ (naṣafa) primarily means to do justice, act equitably, or give someone their due right. It implies fairness and rectitude in dealings, ensuring that what is owed is rendered.
The root QRḌ primarily means "to cut" or "to gnaw," like a rat cutting cloth or a camel chewing its cud.
The root قبض (qbD) primarily means to take or grasp something with the hand, to seize or clutch it. It also extends to taking possession, receiving, or even God taking a soul (causing death).
The root مأي (mAy) primarily signifies the act of drawing water from a well. It can also refer to the water itself, or the place where water is drawn.
A `عَام` (ʿām) is a year, specifically a full cycle of winter and summer.
The root وبل (wbl) refers to the extremity of the scapula, specifically the glenoid cavity, and the surrounding flesh or muscle.
The root بَخَسَ (bakhs) means to diminish, lessen, or make something deficient or faulty. It also means to wrong someone or deprive them of their rights.
The root حظظ primarily means to have good fortune, luck, or a portion allotted by fate.
The root بخل (bkhl) describes someone who is stingy or avaricious. It refers to a person from whom niggardliness is often experienced.
The root 'Emd' primarily refers to a tent pole or a column/pillar. It can also denote a chief or leader, someone relied upon.
The root R-M-Y primarily means to throw or cast something, often with force or intent. It can refer to shooting an arrow, stoning, or even casting a glance.
The root أسو (Asw) primarily conveys the idea of sharing, making equal, or imitating.
The root ندم (ndm) primarily signifies grieving, regretting, or repenting for past actions. It can also imply disliking something.
The root "srq" primarily means to steal, taking something secretly or by artifice.
The root نوق (nwq) relates to daintiness, nicety, and refinement. It implies exceeding the usual in quality, making something good, beautiful, firm, or free from defect.
The root رجف (rjf) describes a state of violent motion, commotion, or agitation, like an earthquake or a trembling hand. It can also refer to thunder rumbling or a fever causing shivering.
The root ضحو (DHw) primarily relates to actions performed during the forenoon (ضُحَى). It describes coming to someone, pasturing animals, or feeding people during this time.
The root كنز (knz) primarily means to bury or hoard treasure, money, or goods. It also refers to pressing or packing things tightly, like dates in a container or filling a bag or waterskin.
The root بكي primarily means to weep or cry, often with tears, due to sorrow, grief, or fear. It can also denote lamenting or mourning. The intensity of the crying can vary.
The root مكث (mkth) means to tarry, stay, or wait. It implies patience and expectation, often in a specific place. It can also mean to loiter or pause.
The root ختم (khtm) primarily refers to sealing or stamping, like with clay or wax.
The root تجر (tjr) primarily refers to a merchant or trader, someone who buys and sells for gain.
The root هبط (hbT) primarily means to descend or go down, like water or a person down a slope. It can also mean to enter a place.
The root أون (Awn) primarily conveys meanings of rest, ease, and tranquility. It also signifies acting gently, proceeding with moderation, and being calm or sedate.
The root برهن (burhān) signifies a clear, decisive, and strong evidence or proof. It's the kind of proof that necessarily implies truth.
The root رغب (rgb) primarily conveys the idea of desire. It can mean to desire something intensely or greedily (رَغِبَ فِيهِ), or to turn away from something, not desiring it (رَغِبَ عَنْهُ).
The root "fyD" relates to overflowing, pouring forth, or gushing out, like water or tears. It also describes abundance, such as God making good abound.
The root كلف (klf) often implies undertaking something difficult or burdensome, either willingly or as a task.
The root بَهَتَ (bht) primarily means to be confounded, perplexed, or amazed, often to the point of being silenced or overcome.
The root سلف (slf) refers to what has gone before, like ancestors or past generations.
The root ZYG primarily means to deviate or swerve from the right path or truth, like a person straying or the sun declining from its zenith.
The root عقر (Eqr) primarily means to wound or hamstring, especially an animal like a camel, often with a sword.
The root أني (Any) is cross-referenced to the root أنى (Anā). To understand its meaning, one should consult the definitions provided under the root أنى.
The root HMM primarily signifies conceiving or purposing something in the mind, often with a strong inclination or desire.
The root خِمْس (khims) primarily refers to the practice of watering camels every fifth day, counting the previous watering day as the first.
The root وهن (whn) signifies weakness, languor, or enervation. It describes being rendered faint, lax, or cowardly, losing energy or resolve. The verb أَوْهَنَهُ means to weaken or unnerve someone.
The root صلب (Slb) primarily denotes hardness, firmness, or rigidity, applying to objects, places, and even abstract concepts like religion or running.
The root فرط (frT) primarily conveys meanings of preceding, sending forth, or neglecting.
The root ضرع (DrE) primarily describes a female animal's udder filling with milk before birth. It also means to lower, humble, or abase someone, often due to hardship like poverty or illness.
The root سقط (sqT) primarily means "to fall" or "to drop," like a physical object or a person fainting. It also describes a fetus being aborted or a person repenting.
The root خضر (khDr) primarily means green, verdant. However, it can also denote dark, blackish, or tawny colors, especially in horses or human complexions.
The root لطف (lTf) means to treat someone with gentleness, kindness, and affection. It implies speaking softly, soothing, and showing good manners. It can also mean to caress or coax someone.
The root عيش (Eysh) relates to life and sustenance. مَعِيشَةٌ (ma'eeshah) means victuals, living, or the means by which one lives, including food and drink.
The root دَلَل (dll) primarily signifies guiding or showing the way, often with kindness.
The root HJB primarily means to prevent, hinder, or conceal. A "hijab" is anything that veils, hides, or forms a barrier, whether physical or abstract.
The root سَتَتَ (sattata) primarily means to cover or conceal something. It implies drawing a veil or screen over an object, making it hidden from view.
The root غبر (gbr) primarily relates to dust and a dusty color. It describes things that are dust-colored, like a wolf or the earth itself.
The root دمر (dmr) describes something small, ignoble, or mean. It can refer to a small, short jerboa, or metaphorically, a small ear.
The root بطش (b-ṭ-sh) primarily means to seize or assault with violence and force. It can also describe taking hold of something strongly or a hand working/laboring.
The root QBR refers to a type of small bird, specifically a lark. It is known by several similar-sounding names, such as qubbar, qubbarah, and qunbura. The plural form is qanabir.
The root سري (sry) primarily means to journey or travel by night. It implies a continuous, often swift, movement during the darkness.
The root ترف (trf) describes someone who lives a life of ease and plenty, often leading to luxury and indulgence.
The root خَسَفَ (khsf) primarily means for the ground to sink or swallow something. It also describes an eye sinking or becoming blind, and the moon or sun undergoing an eclipse.
The root قذف (qadhf) primarily means to throw or cast something, like stones or an arrow. It can also mean to utter truth or conjectures.
The root شَبَه (shbh) primarily means likeness or resemblance. It can refer to something that looks like another, similar to "مثْل" (mithl).
The root نقض (nqD) primarily means to remove a covering, like earth from truffles, or for the earth to reveal plants.
The root ذبح primarily means to cut or split lengthwise. It commonly refers to the ritual slaughter of an animal, making it lawful for consumption.
The root "rjz" primarily describes a camel's disease. It also refers to reciting a specific poetic meter called "rajaz.
The root بقر (bqr) primarily refers to bovine animals, like cows and oxen, both domestic and wild.
The root رعي primarily means to guard, preserve, or pasture animals, implying careful oversight. It extends to observing, considering, or taking care of something, like a promise or a right.
The root عكف (Ekf) primarily means to cleave to something constantly, persevering, or to be intent upon it, often in a place or around an object.
The root بثث (bthth) primarily means to scatter, disperse, or spread something widely. It can also refer to revealing or disclosing a secret, or expressing one's grief and sorrow.
The root "swd" primarily means black, but also signifies greatness or eminence. It can refer to a great, venomous serpent, or metaphorically to dates and water, or even a severe year.
