The root عزم (Ezm) primarily means to determine, resolve, or decide upon something with firmness of heart. It can also mean to strive or exert oneself in an affair.
The root فَيّ (fayy) primarily refers to the return or turning back of something, often after having departed.
The root بَرَزَ (baraza) primarily means to go or come out, to issue forth, or to appear after being hidden.
The root دفع (dfE) primarily means to impel, push, or drive something away, often with force, to remove it from its place. It can also mean to repel or avert something, like evil or harm.
The root NWM primarily signifies sleep, slumber, or being asleep. It can also extend to mean becoming weak, languid, or inactive, similar to the state of sleep.
The root حرق (Hrq) primarily means to burn, often implying destruction or damage by fire. It also describes the act of grinding or grating, like teeth in anger or filing.
The root عبر (Ebr) primarily means to cross or pass over something, like a river or a road. This can extend to metaphorical crossings, such as dying or traveling through life.
The root ف ض ض primarily means to break, burst, or split something open, often with a scattering or dispersing effect. It can refer to breaking a seal, a vessel, or a crowd.
The root خيل (khyl) primarily relates to imaging or fancying something in the mind, often implying illusion or doubt.
The root وَلَجَ (walaja) primarily means "to enter." It describes a person or thing going into a place or another object.
The root "dwm" primarily describes circular motion or stillness within motion. It refers to birds circling, the sun appearing stationary at midday, or eyes rolling.
The root عوج (Ewj) primarily describes something becoming crooked or bent. It can refer to physical objects, like a stick, or abstract concepts, like an affair becoming difficult.
The root صعد (SEd) primarily means to ascend or go upwards, often implying movement towards higher ground or a higher region.
The root ملو primarily signifies filling something completely, to the brim, or to its full capacity. It can also denote a period of time, like a full lifetime, or a full measure of time.
The root جَلَدَ (jld) primarily means to strike or beat, especially the skin, leading to the meaning of flogging. It can also describe a serpent biting or striking with its tail.
The root غنم (ghanim) primarily refers to "booty" or "spoils of war" acquired from non-believers, often by force. It signifies something gained easily.
The root "m-t-r" primarily refers to rain.
The root خوض (khawd) primarily means to wade or pass through water. Tropically, it extends to entering into or plunging through various things, like discourse, affairs, or even false speech.
The root سفل (sfl) primarily means to be or become low, to descend, or to sink downwards. It can describe physical lowness, a low status, or a base and ignoble character.
Rijs (رجس) refers to uncleanness, filth, or anything disliked for its impurity, including sin or actions leading to punishment. It can also mean punishment itself, doubt, or the devil's suggestion.
The root "wqr" primarily relates to heaviness or dullness, especially of hearing, like an ear becoming deaf. It also signifies stillness, resting, or settling in the heart or mind.
The root عتو (Etw) signifies behaving proudly, being immoderate, or revolting from obedience.
The root حلي (Hly) primarily refers to being sweet or becoming sweet, often in taste. It also encompasses the idea of being lawful or permissible, especially in religious contexts.
The root "عنق" (ʿunuq) primarily means "neck." It can refer to the physical neck, but also metaphorically to the beginning of something (like summer or age), a company of people, or chiefs/nobles.
The root ورد (wrd) primarily means "to come to water" or "to arrive at a place," whether entering or not. It extends to "coming" or "being present," like a letter arriving or a fever attacking.
The root عرج (Erj) primarily means to ascend or mount, like climbing stairs. It also describes something becoming high or elevated.
A *ṣaḥīfah* is a written piece of paper, skin, or a book/volume, similar to *kitāb*. Its plural forms are *ṣuḥuf* and *ṣaḥāʼif*.
The root فرج (frj) primarily means to open or make a space between two things, like parting legs or opening a door. It also refers to God removing grief or sorrow.
The root "sfh" primarily means to be unwise, lightwitted, or foolish. It can also describe someone who holds themselves in low esteem or ignores the truth.
The root "SEq" describes being struck by a thunderbolt, leading to swooning, insensibility, or death. It also refers to a loud, vehement sound causing such effects, or a well collapsing.
The root "w-ṣ-l" relates to connection and joining. "Ṣilat al-raḥim" means maintaining kinship ties through kindness.
The root دمو (dmw) primarily refers to "blood." Its original form is debated, with evidence pointing to دَمَوٌ or دَمْىٌ, as seen in its dual and plural forms.
The root Q-D-S signifies holiness, purity, and blessing. It refers to Paradise (Ḥaẓīrat al-Quds) and the Holy Spirit (Rūḥ al-Quds), often identified with Gabriel.
The root ركع primarily means to bow or bend, often due to age. It specifically refers to the bowing in prayer, where one lowers the head and back.
The root غمم (gmm) primarily refers to covering or concealing something, leading to meanings of distress, grief, or anxiety.
The root نيل (nyl) primarily means to obtain, attain, or reach something. It can also signify harming, hurting, or defaming someone, especially an enemy, often through words.
The root ضيع (DyE) primarily relates to perishing, being lost, or neglected. It can refer to an estate or land, especially if neglected, or a craft/occupation by which one earns a living.
The root نقص (nqS) primarily means to decrease, diminish, or become defective. It can describe something losing value or quantity, or someone being deprived of their rights or possessions.
The root سَبَب primarily means a rope or anything by which one ascends or attains an object. It also refers to a means, instrument, or cause for something to happen.
The root زيل (zyl) primarily means to separate or remove something. It also forms the basis for the common phrase "مَا زَالَ" (mā zāla), meaning "he ceased not" or "he continued to do something.
The root عزل (Ezl) primarily refers to the lower spout or outlet of a leather water-bag (مَزَادَة), from which water is poured.
The root يمم primarily means to go or direct oneself towards a place or person, often with intention.
The root خَبِيثٌ (khabīth) describes something bad, corrupt, or impure, whether physically or morally. It can refer to unpleasant tastes/odors, unlawful things, or wicked people/actions.
The root كفل (kfl) means to be responsible, accountable, or a surety for something or someone. It implies guaranteeing property or ensuring a person's presence for legal matters.
The root غيظ (ghayz) signifies intense, often hidden, anger or rage, more potent than غضب (ghaḍab). It can be a deep-seated fury, sometimes affecting those powerless to act.
The root Twl generally means to be or become long, tall, or extended, referring to objects, time, or even anxiety. It can also mean to exceed or surpass someone in height or merit.
The root جَارٌ (jār) primarily means a neighbor, someone living nearby. It also extends to mean a protector, one who grants refuge, or someone seeking protection.
The root جَبَرَ (jabr) primarily means to set a broken bone. Tropically, it extends to restoring someone from poverty to wealth or competence, or generally putting something into a sound state.
The root حيق (Hyq) primarily means to surround or encompass, specifically in relation to evil or punishment.
The root قهر (qahr) means to overcome, conquer, or overpower someone or something. It also implies abasing, oppressing, or forcing someone, as seen in the Quran (93:9) regarding orphans.
The root ASL refers to the foundational part of something, like the root of a tree or the base of a mountain. It also signifies origin, source, or lineage, as in a person's ancestry.
The root ضحك (DHk) primarily means "to laugh," expressing joy or wonder. It can also describe the opening of flowers, the glistening of water, or the bursting of a palm spathe.
The root "rhq" primarily means to come upon, reach, or draw near to something, often implying an encompassing or overtaking action.
The root زلف (zlf) primarily conveys the meaning of nearness, closeness, or proximity, whether in terms of physical distance, rank, or status. It can also refer to a portion or division of the night.
The root جَدَدَ (jadd) primarily means to cut or to make something new. It signifies renewal, making something fresh, or a new path/way. It can also refer to a new garment or a new fortune.
The root فَرَر (f-r-r) primarily signifies fleeing, running away, or escaping from something. It implies a rapid movement to get away, often due to fear or to avoid an undesirable situation.
The root عون (Ewn) primarily means aid, help, or assistance. It can refer to the act of helping or to a helper/assistant, whether singular or plural, male or female.
The root وَقَدَ (waqada) primarily describes fire burning brightly or fiercely, blazing, or flaming. It can also refer to something shining or glistening.
The root طَوْر (Twr) primarily denotes "time" or "occasion." It also signifies "state," "condition," or "manner," as in the creation of humans through various stages.
The root "Hrth" primarily means to gain or acquire wealth, often through diligent labor. It also refers to tilling land for sowing, and metaphorically, to working for one's afterlife.
The root أيد (Ayd) signifies anything that strengthens, guards, or protects. It can refer to a fortification, a place of refuge, or even the wings of an army.
The root سحب (sHb) primarily refers to "clouds" (سحاب), so called because they are drawn along in the air. The word can be singular or plural, masculine or feminine.
The root حرر (Hrr) primarily signifies setting free, emancipating, or liberating someone or something from bondage, slavery, or restriction.
The root صوم (Swm) primarily means to abstain, often from food, drink, and coitus, as in fasting during Ramadan. It can also mean abstaining from speech, as in Mary's vow.
The root "khwn" signifies unfaithfulness, treachery, or betrayal of trust, contrasting with trustworthiness (amānah).
لغو (laghw) refers to speech or actions that are vain, idle, or of no real account. It signifies something unprofitable or useless, often without serious intent.
The root "byE" primarily means to exchange property, encompassing both selling and buying. It can also mean to offer something for sale.
The root عنب (Enb) primarily refers to "grapes" (عِنَبٌ), the fruit of the grapevine. It can also tropically signify the "grape-vine" itself, as seen in the Quran.
The root حرب (Hrb) primarily means "war" or "battle." It is usually feminine, but can be masculine. It can also describe a "warrior" or someone "vehement in war.
The root طرف (Trf) primarily signifies the extremity or end of something, like a sword's tip or a rope's end. It also denotes a side, region, or a portion of a thing.
The root زبر (zbr) primarily means to case a well with stones, or to build one part upon another. It also means to chide or restrain someone with rough speech, preventing them from an action.
The root حرج (Hrj) conveys the idea of narrowness, tightness, or confinement. It can describe a physical space, a feeling of distress or doubt in one's heart, or being in a difficult situation.
The root "drk" signifies reaching, overtaking, or coming up with something or someone. It implies continuity, uninterrupted sequence, or successive arrival.
The root WDY primarily means to pay blood-money or compensation for a life. It also refers to the act of giving or presenting something, often as a gift or offering.
The root قصر (q-ṣ-r) primarily means to be or become short, or to fall short of something. It can describe an arrow missing its target, a person lacking power or ability, or money being insufficient.
The root طبع (TbE) primarily means to seal, stamp, or imprint, like sealing a letter or coining money.
The root ط ر ق (Trq) primarily means to strike or beat, like knocking on a door or beating wool. It also refers to coming by night, especially to one's family, and a stallion covering a she-camel.
The root يأس (yAs) primarily means to despair or lose hope. It signifies a state of hopelessness, often in relation to something desired or expected.
The root شيع (shyE) primarily means to follow or cause to follow. It describes a pastor calling camels to follow, or urging sheep.
The root "shml" primarily means to include or encompass something, like an event affecting everyone. It also describes covering something, like with a garment, or a she-camel conceiving.
The root نَصَحَ (nSH) primarily means to advise sincerely, directing someone to what is good. It also conveys purity, genuineness, and thoroughness, like pure honey or sincere repentance.
The root "jml" primarily refers to a male camel, specifically a full-grown one. It can also be used generically for camels or even metaphorically for a woman's husband or tall palm trees.
The root عذر primarily means to excuse or free from blame. It can also mean to be faulty, deserving punishment, or to aid someone.
The root وكأ (wkA) is primarily understood through its eighth form, اتّكأ (ittakaʾa). This form signifies leaning or reclining upon something for support or rest.

The root HSY primarily means to count or reckon, often implying a precise and comprehensive enumeration. It can also refer to knowing or comprehending something fully, as if counting its every detail.
The root شفق (shfq) primarily relates to fear, often with a sense of solicitude or compassion.
The root نطق (nTq) primarily means "to speak" or "to utter." It can describe singing birds, a deenár (coin), or a rational root in arithmetic.
The root أبي (aby) primarily means to refuse, reject, or decline something, often with a sense of aversion or disdain.
The root "rhb" relates to fear and awe. "Rahbānīyah" refers to monasticism or asceticism, often associated with Christian devotees.
The root ESw primarily refers to a staff or stick, originally 'عَصَوٌ'. It's used metaphorically for unity, as in 'collecting people together'.
The root بكر (bkr) primarily means to go forth or come early in the morning, between daybreak and sunrise. It can also tropically mean to hasten to something at any time, morning or evening.
The root طمع (TmE) primarily means to covet or desire something eagerly, often with a sense of greed or inordinate longing.
The root "nbdh" primarily means to cast or throw away something deemed worthless, often used in the Quran. It can also mean to disregard a covenant or neglect an affair.
The root قنت (qnt) primarily signifies obedience, especially constant obedience to God.
Hnf describes someone who inclines to a right state, especially from false religion to true religion.
The root HSR primarily means to remove or uncover something. It also describes becoming tired or fatigued, whether a beast from travel or the eye from prolonged looking.
The root LHM relates to joining or closing things, like patching a hole in a garment or consolidating wounds.
The root "sfr" primarily means to sweep or clear away, like wind dispersing dust or clouds. It also describes a woman uncovering her face or the sun rising.
The root عسر (Esr) primarily signifies difficulty, hardship, or intricacy in affairs.
The root "byD" primarily refers to an egg, especially an ostrich egg, due to its whiteness. It can also metaphorically describe a helmet, a testicle, or the core of something.
The root "rbS" means to expect, await, or tarry while expecting something. It implies looking forward to an event, whether good or bad, to befall someone or something.
The root خُطْبَةٌ (khuṭbah) refers to a formal speech, sermon, or oration, often delivered in public. It's like an exhortation or admonition, similar to a modern-day sermon.
The root كنن primarily means to cover, conceal, or protect something, often by putting it into a shelter or hidden place.
The root طمأن (TmAn) primarily means to be or become quiet, tranquil, or at rest, especially after movement or disturbance.
The root مَسَحَ (masaha) primarily means to wipe or pass one's hand over something, often to remove wetness or dirt. It can also mean to measure land, to cut or strike, or to anoint with oil.
The root طين (Tyn) primarily means to plaster or seal with clay or mud. It can also metaphorically refer to God creating someone with a good disposition, or a person performing their work well.
The root Hwr relates to returning or circling. A "mahārah" can be a mother-of-pearl shell, a place where water collects, or a cavity in the body like the ear or hip.
The root عِصَامٌ (ʿiṣām) refers to a tie or cord, like those used for water-skins or bags, to secure their contents or for carrying. It also denotes anything that provides protection or preservation.
The root جبي (jby) primarily refers to "ginger" (زَنْجَبِيلٌ), a well-known plant root with medicinal properties, often used dried.
The root HSn relates to protection and chastity. It describes preserving oneself from unlawful acts, especially for women.
The root Hlf refers to a type of tall, coarse grass that grows near water, known as *halfa'*. It's rough to the touch and sometimes eaten by animals.
The root لوم (lwm) primarily means to blame, censure, or reprehend someone for something. It signifies finding fault or expressing disapproval.
The root جحد (jHd) primarily means to deny or disacknowledge something, whether knowing the truth or not.
The root ضيق (Dyq) primarily means to be or become narrow or strait, the opposite of spacious.
The root زرع primarily means "to sow" or "to cultivate land." It can also mean "to plant trees" or, tropically, "to sow love.
The root خرر primarily describes the act of falling down, often with a sound like a crash or rustle.
The root ETw primarily means to take or handle something, often with the hand. It can also imply contending in taking or giving, or standing on tiptoes to reach.
The root شقو (shqw) describes struggling or contending with someone, often in a competitive or adversarial way. It implies striving to overcome or surpass another, or enduring hardship together.
Sijjeen refers to a place where the records of the wicked are kept, often described as a valley in Hell or a stone beneath the seventh earth. It can also mean a register of evil deeds.
The root سلك (slk) means to travel, go along, or enter a path or place. It also means to insert or cause something to enter into another, like threading a needle or water entering springs.
The root نطف (nTf) refers to a type of sweetmeat, similar to "qubbayṭā." It's a confection, often sticky or syrupy.
The root صَفَف primarily means to arrange things in a row or line, to set them in order, or to draw them up in ranks.
The root فدي (fdy) primarily means to ransom or redeem someone, often by giving something in exchange to free them from captivity, punishment, or a difficult situation.
The root رَأَفَ (ra'afa) primarily signifies having intense, tender compassion and mercy. It denotes a profound and active pity, often leading to a desire to alleviate suffering.
The root وَقَتَ primarily means to determine, define, or limit something, especially in terms of time. It signifies appointing a specific time for an event or action.
The primary meaning of خَلَل (khall) refers to a gap, interstice, or space between things. It can also denote a defect, flaw, or disorder, often arising from such a gap or interruption.
The root صغر (Sgr) primarily means to be small or little, either in size or age. It also conveys the sense of being vile, base, or ignominious, losing respect or dignity.
The root شهو (shhw) primarily signifies intense desire or longing, often for things that gratify the senses. It can refer to necessary appetites like hunger, or to excessive, blameworthy desires.
The root غلم (glm) primarily refers to a young man, boy, or youth, often specifically when his mustache is beginning to grow. It can also denote a male slave or a hireling/servant.
The root فوه (fwh) primarily refers to the mouth (فَمٌ). Its plural is أَفْوَاهٌ. The word فَمٌ is considered a transformation of فوه, where the ه was replaced by م.
The root غلظ (ghalaza) describes something that is thick, coarse, or rough, whether physically or figuratively.
The root غلل primarily means to enter or penetrate, like water seeping through trees.
The root بغت (bgt) signifies something happening suddenly, unexpectedly, or by surprise. It implies an unforeseen event or an abrupt encounter.
The root خزن (khzn) primarily means to store, lay up, or preserve something, like property, often in a storeroom. It can also mean to conceal a secret or to withhold a gift.
The root "njm" primarily refers to a star or constellation, especially the Pleiades. It can also describe sprouts emerging from roots, resembling large needles.
A مِكْيَالٌ (mikyal) is a device used to measure grains like corn. It refers to a specific capacity measure, similar to how we use terms like "bushel" or "liter" today.
The root صيح (SyH) primarily means to raise one's voice, call out, or cry aloud, often vehemently. It can also metaphorically describe being frightened or perishing.
The root صمم (Smm) primarily conveys the idea of being deaf or having a blocked ear. It also extends to meaning firmness, resolution, or being determined, as if one is deaf to distractions.
The root "frD" primarily refers to a mark or incision, like a notch in a bow for the string. It also signifies something made obligatory or binding by God, for which one is punished if neglected.
The root كفف (kff) primarily means to restrain, hold back, or prevent something. It implies stopping an action or keeping something from happening. It can also refer to being sufficient or enough.
The root فقر (fqr) primarily relates to a hollow or well, often for planting or water. It also describes a person with a broken or diseased spine.
The root رجم primarily means to throw stones, leading to meanings like stoning to death, driving away, or reviling.
The root عشو (Eshw) primarily relates to eating the evening meal or pasturing animals at night. It also describes seeking guidance by firelight, or turning away from something.
The root ثوي primarily means to reside, dwell, or remain in a place. It implies settling down and taking up abode, often for an extended period.
The root WZR primarily means to bear a heavy burden, often referring to the burden of sin. It's used in the Quran to convey that no soul bears another's burden of sin.
The root وَصَفَ (wasafa) refers to describing or attributing qualities. A صِفَة (sifah) is a quality, attribute, or description of a thing's state.
The root بدأ (bdA) primarily means "to begin" or "to do something first." It is used in phrases like "to begin with" or "to do something from the beginning.
The root رَسَا primarily describes something becoming stationary, firm, or fixed, like a mountain or a ship anchoring. It also refers to establishing agreement between people or relating a tradition.
The root "swm" primarily means to go, seek, or roam freely, like cattle pasturing. It also signifies passing quickly, or birds circling.
The root جهر (jhr) primarily means to be or make something plain, apparent, or conspicuous, whether visually or audibly.
The root مهد (mhd) means to make something plain, even, or smooth, like preparing a bed. It also signifies preparing good things for oneself or establishing a high station for someone.
The root ركب (rkb) primarily means to ride or mount something, like a beast or a ship.
The root RBW primarily means "to increase" or "to grow." It describes things like property increasing (sometimes through usury), a child growing up, or ground swelling after rain.
The root سنن (snn) primarily refers to a way, course, or rule that is followed, whether good or bad. It implies a beaten track or a customary practice that has been established and is adhered to.
The root شَكَّ (shakka) primarily means to doubt or be uncertain about something. It implies a state of hesitation or wavering belief, often due to a lack of clear evidence or conviction.
The root LHW relates to the uvula, the fleshy part hanging in the back of the throat. It can also refer to the area between the tongue and the roof of the mouth, or the furthest part of the mouth.
The root فَأَد (faʾada) primarily refers to the heart, specifically the organ itself. It can also denote the intellect or understanding, as the heart was considered the seat of these faculties.
سَوْرَةٌ (sawrah) refers to a sudden rush or assault, like wine to the head or venom. It can also describe an outburst of anger, the intensity of cold, or the might of a ruler.
The root خشع (khashaa) means to be humble, submissive, or lowly. It implies a state of stillness, often in the voice or eyes, and can also refer to fear, especially in prayer.

The root بوأ (bwA) is not directly defined here. Instead, it points to other entries. "جُوْزُ بَوَّا" refers to the entry for "جوز" (jawz), and "خَيْرُ بَوَّآءُ" refers to the entry for "خير" (khayr).
The root عَلَنَ (ʿalana) primarily means to make something open, manifest, or public. It can refer to revealing an affair, making an event known, or even a woman confessing an act.
The root مَلَلَ (mll) primarily signifies weariness, boredom, or becoming tired of something. It implies a state of being fed up or disgusted, leading to abandonment or neglect.
The root صَفَا (ṣafā) primarily refers to smooth, hard stones or rocks, often large and barren. A single stone is called صَفَاةٌ (ṣafāh). The term also denotes a specific location in Mecca.
The root لَبَبَ (lbb) primarily refers to the breast or chest, specifically the part where a necklace rests.
The root حبط (HbT) primarily describes a beast's belly swelling from unwholesome food, leading to sickness or death.
The root نقم (nqm) primarily means to take vengeance or inflict penal retribution upon someone for their actions. It also conveys the sense of punishing someone.
The root غدو (gdw) primarily refers to the early part of the morning, specifically the time between daybreak prayer and sunrise. It can also broadly mean morning, before or after sunrise.
The root عتد (Etd) refers to preparation and readiness. عَتَادٌ signifies apparatus, implements, or equipage, especially for war, like weapons and beasts.
The root زعم (z-'-m) primarily means "to assert" or "to claim," often implying doubt or uncertainty about the truthfulness of the statement.
The root نَفَرَ (nafara) primarily means to take fright and flee, like a wild animal. It extends to shying away from something, being averse to it, or receding/withdrawing.
The root مكن (mkn) means to establish, settle, or assign a place to someone. It also signifies giving someone mastery, dominion, or power over something, enabling them to control or possess it.
The root سطر (sTr) primarily refers to a "line" of writing, a book, or a row of things like buildings or trees. It can also mean "writing" itself.
The root "سوق" (sāq) primarily refers to the shank, the part of the leg between the knee and foot. It can also denote the trunk of a tree.
The root عوذ (Ewdh) means to seek protection, refuge, or preservation, often with God. It implies confiding in someone for safety.
The root خفف primarily means to be light or to make something light. It can refer to something being light in weight, swift in movement, or easy to bear.
The root منع (mnE) means to be prevented, to refrain voluntarily, or to be inaccessible. It implies resistance, refusal, or something being impossible.
The root شرق primarily describes the rising and shining of the sun, often from the east.
The root "gharb" relates to distance and the west, as in sunset. It also describes sharpness, like a sword's edge or a keen mind.
The root شَهْر (shahr) primarily refers to the new moon, visible and conspicuous. From this, it evolved to mean a lunar month, a known period of days made manifest by the moon.
The primary meaning of رأس relates to the head of anything, whether physical or metaphorical.
The root خَصْم (khSm) primarily refers to the side, edge, or corner of an object, like a load or a bed. It can also denote the extremity of a water-bag or the corners of a cloud.
The root ثَبَتَ (thbt) means to make something firm, stable, or permanent. It can also mean to establish a fact, prove something, or render someone unable to move.
The root S-W-R primarily means to incline, lean, or turn something. It can also mean to cut or dissect.
The term "مِنْ لَدُنْ" (min ladun) means "from the time of" or "from the presence of.
Awb primarily means to return, whether a person to a place or from a journey, or the sun setting. It also signifies returning to one's family at night or coming to water to drink at night.
A "hizb" is a group of people united by a common purpose or event, like a party, faction, or companions. It also refers to a set portion of the Quran or prayer one recites regularly.
The root حجر (Hjr) primarily means "forbidden" or "prohibited." It can refer to something unlawful, inviolable, or sacred.
The root دَبَب primarily refers to slow, soft, or gentle movement, like a child crawling or an old person walking. It can also describe the movement of insects or small creatures.
The root F-K-R refers to deep thought, contemplation, or mental examination. It involves using the mind to understand something clearly, often by arranging known ideas to discover new insights.
The root غوي (gwy) primarily signifies going astray, deviating from the right path, or being misguided. It implies error, delusion, or acting foolishly, often leading to ruin or failure.
The root نفخ (nfkh) primarily means to blow, like blowing with one's mouth or into a trumpet. It can also describe inflation, such as food causing bloating or a devil inflating one's nose with pride.

The root ط-ل-ع (ṭ-l-ʿ) primarily signifies "to rise" or "to appear," like the sun, moon, or stars. It also describes anything emerging or becoming visible, such as a child's tooth or plants sprouting.
The root نوب (nwb) signifies repetition, returning, or coming by turns. It describes things happening time after time, like a wild ass visiting water or a person returning to God in repentance.
The root حذر (Hdhr) conveys caution, wariness, and vigilance. It describes someone who is prepared, on guard, or fearful.
The root ثمن (thmn) primarily refers to the number "eight.
The root M-N-Y primarily signifies measuring, estimating, or determining something. It also relates to decreeing, appointing, or ordaining, often with a sense of predestination or fate.

The root Emr relates to life, habitation, and flourishing. It describes living long, a place becoming inhabited or prosperous, and maintaining or building something. It also refers to worshipping God.
The root أَلِفَ (alifa) means to become familiar with, accustomed to, or to cleave to something or someone. It also implies love or affection.
The root بلد (bld) primarily refers to a country, region, or town. It can also denote a desert or extensive tract of land. Figuratively, it describes separation or a desolate place.
The root مري (mry) primarily means to stroke or rub, especially to draw forth milk from a she-camel.
The root رشد (rshd) signifies taking or following a right way or course, whether in general affairs or religious belief. It implies guidance towards truth and rectitude.
The root نكح (nkH) primarily means "to marry" or "to take in marriage" in the Quran, though it can also refer to sexual intercourse. Its usage in the Quran exclusively denotes marriage.
The root سعر primarily means to kindle or stir fire, making it burn brightly. Tropically, it extends to igniting war, exciting mischief, or causing widespread harm.
The root فتي primarily denotes youthfulness, being a young man or woman, or a youth. It also carries meanings of being new, fresh, or recently made.
The root صنع (ṣanaʿa) means to make, craft, or manufacture something skillfully. It also refers to doing a favor or a deed, whether good or bad.
The root فطر (f-ṭ-r) primarily means to cleave or split.
The root فكه (fkh) primarily relates to eating fruit, enjoying it, or even abstaining from it. In the Quran, it can imply irony, wondering, or repenting.
The root م-ش-ي primarily means to walk or go on foot. It can also imply proceeding, journeying, or moving forward in a general sense.
The root كتم (ktm) primarily means to conceal or suppress something, especially a secret. It implies keeping information hidden from others.
The root لَبَسَ (labasa) primarily means "to put on or wear" a garment or armor. Tropically, it extends to "living with people" or "tolerating someone.
The root خ-ط-أ primarily signifies making a mistake or error, whether intentionally or unintentionally. It encompasses missing the mark, deviating from the correct path, or acting incorrectly.
The root "snw" primarily means to water or irrigate land, often using animals. It also describes fire or lightning shining brightly, or rising high.
The root تَمَمَ primarily means to complete or perfect something, bringing it to its end or desired state. It implies making something whole, full, or faultless.
The root رقب (rqb) signifies watching, guarding, or observing. A رَقِيبٌ is a watcher, guardian, or overseer.
The root H-D-D primarily means to define, limit, or set boundaries. It can refer to making something distinct or sharp, like a sword's edge.
The root حلم (Hlm) primarily means "to dream" or "to see a vision in sleep." It also signifies reaching puberty or virility.
The root "drj" primarily refers to a path, road, or way, whether literal or figurative. It can describe a physical route, a course of action, or even a means to an end.
The root نخل (nkhl) means to clear, sift, or take the best part of something. It implies a process of selection, choosing the finest or most excellent portion.
The root "nzʿ" primarily means to pull out, extract, or remove something. It also conveys the sense of yearning or longing for something, often with an inclination towards it.
The root فقه (fqh) primarily means to understand, comprehend, and know, especially in matters of religious law.
The root لَعِبَ (laʿiba) primarily means to play, sport, or jest, contrasting with seriousness.
The root كشف (kashafa) means to reveal, uncover, or disclose something. It can also imply acting openly with someone, showing clear enmity, or making war openly.
The root حمم (Hmm) primarily refers to blackness or being intensely black. It can also denote destiny, fate, or a decreed matter, often with an implication of something inevitable or predetermined.
The root نشر (n-sh-r) primarily means to spread or open something, like a garment or news. It also refers to scattering or dispersing.
The root غضب (ghadiba) primarily means to be angry with someone. It can also mean to be angry on behalf of someone, or to be angry for God's sake.
The root ربع (rbE) primarily relates to the concept of "four" or "fourth." It can mean taking a fourth part, becoming the fourth in a group, or twisting something with four strands.
The root فجر primarily means to cleave or cut open, like breaking a dam for water to flow. This extends to opening a path for water or blood.
The root وصي (w-ṣ-y) primarily means to enjoin, command, or make a will. It involves giving a charge or instruction, often with a sense of care or guardianship.
The root طلق (Tlq) primarily means to loose, set free, or let go. It applies to releasing captives, untying animals, or allowing freedom of movement.
The root بَقِيَ primarily means to remain, stay, or continue to exist after others have gone. It signifies permanence, endurance, or a remnant.
The root غرر (grr) primarily signifies being deceived or deluded, often by outward appearances or false hopes.
The root فَرِح (frH) describes being joyful, glad, or happy. It can also mean well-pleased or content.
The root سرف (srf) primarily means to be ignorant, unmindful, or negligent of something, or to miss it. It can also describe a worm eating leaves or wood, or metaphorically, food becoming cankered.
The root أثر (Athr) refers to a trace, relic, or sign left behind, like a footprint or the remains of a house.
The root WZN relates to weight. A "wāzin" object is heavy or of full, complete weight, like a "dirham wāzin" which is a full-weight dirham.
The root "thmr" primarily refers to the fruit of trees, whether edible or not. Tropically, it can mean wealth, gold/silver, children, or the profit/outcome of something.
The root YTM primarily means to make someone an orphan, specifically by causing them to lose their father. This action renders a child fatherless.
The root أذي primarily signifies harm, hurt, or annoyance, whether physical or mental.
The root "trb" primarily refers to "dust" or "earth." It can denote fine, dry particles or moist soil.
The root قسط (qsT) primarily signifies equity and justice, often used as an adjective meaning "equitable" or "just.
The root "whb" primarily means to give something as a free, disinterested gift, without expectation of compensation.
The root وَقَعَ (waqaʿa) primarily means "to fall" or "to happen." It can describe an event taking place, someone falling into a situation (like a snare), or something landing on a surface.
The root عرب (Erb) primarily signifies clarity and distinctness in speech, particularly in Arabic. It encompasses speaking plainly, without error, and expressing meanings perspicuously.

The root مَرَض (marad) primarily means physical illness or sickness. Tropically, it refers to spiritual or mental ailments like doubt, hypocrisy, weakness of belief, or a corrupted state of the heart.
The root شري primarily means to buy or sell, often implying an exchange or trade. It can also denote being sharp or quick, like a horse, or having a fiery temperament.
The root غرق (gharaqa) primarily means to drown or sink. It can also mean to annul good deeds, to be overwhelmed by people or beasts, or to outstrip someone.

The root نبت primarily means "to grow" or "sprout," referring to plants emerging from the ground. It can also describe land producing vegetation or, metaphorically, a girl's breast becoming prominent.
The root ذلل primarily signifies being low, humble, or submissive, often in a gentle or easy manner. It can describe something made easy to use, like a path, or a person made subservient.
A "thawb" is a garment, typically a single piece of cloth worn by men, not tailored from multiple pieces.
The root فحش (fHsh) describes anything excessive, immoderate, or beyond proper bounds. It refers to actions or speech that are foul, evil, abominable, or unseemly.
The root سرع (srE) primarily means to quicken or hasten. It can be used transitively, like "he quickened his pace," or intransitively, meaning "he made haste.
The root بسط (bsT) primarily means to spread, expand, or extend something. It can refer to physical objects like garments or hands, or abstract concepts like sustenance or justice.
The root مكر (mkr) primarily means to practice deceit, guile, or circumvention, often with the intent to harm clandestinely.
The root كود (kwd) primarily means "to be near to doing something." When used affirmatively, it implies the action was almost done but not completed.
The root "سبع" (sbE) primarily refers to the number seven. It's used for counting, like "seven men" or "seven women.
The root عدل (Edl) primarily means to act justly and equitably. It also conveys the sense of turning aside or deviating from a path, whether literally or figuratively from the truth.
The root بوب (bwb) primarily refers to a "door" or "gate," a place of entrance, or the object used to close it. It can also metaphorically mean a "means of access" or "attainment" to something.
The root سقي primarily means to give or get water, to drink, or to irrigate. It encompasses actions like watering plants, providing drink to people or animals, and drawing water.
The root ثني primarily means to fold, bend, or turn something back. It also conveys the idea of repeating or doing something a second time.
The root وعظ (wEzh) means to exhort, admonish, or warn someone, often by reminding them of consequences or divine reward and punishment.
The root ج-ه-ل primarily signifies ignorance, lack of knowledge, or acting foolishly due to not knowing.
The root خزي primarily means to be or become put to shame, disgraced, or abased. It implies humiliation, ignominy, or contempt, often as a consequence of wrongdoing or failure.
The root عجب (ʿajaba) primarily conveys the idea of wonder or astonishment at something strange or unfamiliar. It can describe a feeling or a thing that causes wonder.
The root مسك (msk) primarily means to hold, retain, or withhold. It can refer to grasping something firmly, restraining someone, or abstaining from an action.
The root طير (ṭyr) primarily refers to anything that flies, like a bird or insect. It can also denote an omen, either good or bad, or one's fortune or destiny.
The root وَضَعَ (w-ḍ-ʿ) primarily means to put or lay down, the opposite of lifting up. It can also mean to give birth, impose or remit a tax, or cease hostilities.
The root لسن (lisān) primarily refers to the tongue. However, it can also describe the projecting part of a sandal, the tongue of a balance, or even news/tidings.
The root "Hwl" primarily signifies change, alteration, or transformation from one state to another. It can describe things shifting, moving, or becoming crooked.
The root أدم (Adm) primarily refers to seasoned food, often with a sauce or condiment. It also denotes tanned animal skin or hide, and metaphorically, the surface of the earth or sky.
The root مَنَنَ primarily means to cut or break something. It also conveys the idea of weakness or failing strength.
The root شقق primarily means to cleave, split, or tear something apart, creating a fissure or division. It can also imply difficulty or hardship, as if something is being split open with effort.
The root حضر (HDr) primarily means to be present, to come, or to arrive, often in contrast to being absent. It can refer to a person being present at a place or event, or a time or thing arriving.
The root فلك (flk) primarily refers to the celestial sphere or orbit of stars, often imagined as a material vault.
The root "b-t-n" primarily refers to the belly or abdomen, the inner part of the body. It also extends to mean the inside or interior of anything, like a valley or city.
The root قَصَص (q-ṣ-ṣ) primarily means to follow tracks or footsteps, to narrate or relate a story, or to cut hair.
The root سَيْر (syr) primarily means to go, travel, or proceed, by day or night. It applies to people, animals, and even ships (metaphorically).
The root صلي (Sly) primarily means to be exposed to fire or heat, to roast, or to burn.
The root عجز primarily refers to old age and weakness, especially in women. It can also describe old wine or specific parts of a sword.
The root نشأ primarily means to originate, grow, or rise up. It signifies the beginning of existence, development, or an upward movement.
The root غشو (gshw) primarily means to cover or conceal, like night covering the earth. It also signifies something coming upon or overwhelming, such as an event or drowsiness.

The root طهر (Thr) primarily means to cleanse or purify oneself, often with water, like performing ablution. It can also metaphorically mean to remove oneself from impurities, sins, or ignoble habits.
The root شجر (shjr) primarily refers to trees, shrubs, or plants with a trunk/stem. It can also metaphorically denote a person's lineage or origin.
The root شَفَع (shafaʿa) primarily means to make something a pair or to join one thing to another. This can refer to making a single item into a pair, or a she-camel having a second offspring.
The root عشر (Eshr) primarily means "ten." It's used as عَشَرَةٌ for masculine nouns and عَشْرٌ for feminine nouns.
The root H-J-J primarily signifies the act of going or repairing to a place or person, often with the intention of visiting or performing a pilgrimage.
The root HWN describes something that is low, base, vile, or contemptible. It can also mean something is easy or gentle. In the Quran, it often refers to a state of humiliation or insignificance.
The root جحم (jHm) relates to intense heat and burning. It describes live coals, a fiercely hot place, and metaphorically, the intense part or vehemence of battle.
The root قعد (q-ʿ-d) primarily means "to sit," often implying sitting down after standing, or sitting for a duration. It can also mean "to remain," "to abstain from," or "to become.
The root "Anth" describes land that is plain, soft, and fertile, producing abundant vegetation.
The root ثقل (thql) primarily means "to be heavy" or "weighty." It can refer to physical weight, but also to things that are ideally heavy, like good deeds outweighing bad ones.
The root قمر (qmr) primarily means to contend for stakes or wagers, often in games of chance, and to overcome an opponent in such a contest.
The root HwT primarily means to guard, protect, or take care of someone or something, often with diligent attention. It can also imply surrounding or encompassing.
The root جدل (jdl) primarily refers to a braided or twisted object, like a waist-wrap.
The root هجر (hjr) primarily means to cut off, forsake, or abandon someone or something. It also refers to the act of migrating, especially from one's home or country to another.
The root "rjw" primarily means to hope for something, often implying a fear of not attaining it. It can also mean to fear, especially when used with a negative.
The root جند (jnd) primarily refers to an army, military force, or soldiers. It can also denote any kind or species of creatures, especially those used by God to achieve His purposes.
The root لبث (lbth) primarily means to tarry, remain, or stay in a place. It also conveys the sense of pausing, waiting, or being patient.
The root فوز (fwz) primarily means to attain good fortune, succeed, or win. It also conveys the sense of escaping harm or becoming safe.
The root مَدَنَ (madana) relates to dwelling in a city or being urbanized. A "madīnah" is a city.
The root يقن (yqn) primarily means to know something with certainty or to be sure of it. It implies a deep, intuitive, or inferential understanding, similar to "to ascertain" or "to verify."
The root خلو (khlw) primarily means to be empty, vacant, or alone. It describes a place without occupants or a person being by themselves.
The root برأ (brA) primarily means to be clear or free from something, like recovering from illness or being absolved from debt.
أَبَد (abad) refers to an absolute or long, unlimited time, often translated as "eternity" or "forever." It contrasts with أَزَل (azal), which signifies time without beginning.
The root W-D-D primarily signifies love, affection, and desire. It encompasses wishing for something to happen or for someone to be in a certain state. It can also denote a strong, enduring fondness.
The root سعي (sEy) primarily means to walk, run, or go quickly, often with effort or intention.
The root "thlth" relates to the number three. It can mean to take a third of something, or to be/make a third person/thing in a group.
The root عسي (Esy) primarily denotes hope or expectation, often with an element of difficulty or uncertainty. It can also imply a near occurrence or the act of being about to do something.
The root غلب (ghalaba) primarily means to overcome, conquer, or gain ascendancy over someone or something. It implies prevailing in power, force, or influence.

The root د-ر-ي primarily means to know, perceive, or be aware of something, often implying a degree of seeking or finding out. It can also convey the sense of being skilled or experienced in a matter.
The root مَدَد primarily signifies extension, stretching, or prolonging something, whether physically or metaphorically. It can also mean to supply or provide assistance, often in a continuous flow.
The root وثق (wthq) conveys securing oneself or something, often through a bond or firm action. It implies taking precautions, ensuring stability, or establishing trust.
The root "bdw" primarily means "to appear" or "become manifest." It also describes an opinion arising or changing, or people going out to the desert.

حَيْثُ (haythu) is an indeclinable adverb of place, meaning "where." It typically precedes a proposition (a phrase with a verb or noun). While primarily denoting place, it can sometimes signify "when.
The root هود (hwd) primarily relates to becoming Jewish or teaching Judaism. It also describes gentle, slow movement or speech, like a soft voice or leisurely pace.
The root "رفع" (rafaʿa) primarily means to raise, elevate, or uplift something, often in contrast to lowering it.
The root وسع (w-s-ʿ) conveys the idea of becoming ample, abundant, or expansive. It describes widening, spreading out, or taking a broad range in affairs, bounty, or even the meaning of words.
The root صير (Syr) primarily means "to become" or "to attain a state/condition." It also signifies "to return to a place" or "to come to an end.
The root S-R-F generally means to turn something away, back, or aside from its course, or to shift it from one state to another.
The root نَصَبَ (naṣaba) primarily means to set up, erect, or raise something. It also describes a specific type of Arabic chanting or singing.
The root كيد (kyd) primarily means to deceive, beguile, or circumvent someone, often with ill intent or clandestinely.
The root أفك (Afk) primarily means to turn something away or back, often implying deceit or falsehood. It can describe being turned away from truth or good, or someone lying or causing others to lie.
The root عمي primarily means blindness, both physical and metaphorical. It refers to being unable to see or perceive, often implying a lack of guidance or understanding.
The root برر (brr) primarily signifies being good, righteous, or pious. It encompasses truthfulness, extensive goodness, and dutifulness, especially towards parents.
The root خَلَص (khalaṣa) refers to something becoming clear, pure, or refined. It's often used for clarifying butter by removing impurities, or for the best, most essential part of something.
The root شَرَر primarily refers to sparks of fire, or small, scattered pieces that fly off from a burning object.
The root عفو (Efw) primarily means to efface or obliterate, like traces or dwellings. From this, it extends to forgiving sins, meaning to efface them.
The root ظَلَلَ primarily means to shade or cover, providing protection from the sun or heat. It can also imply being in the shade, or something that is dark or obscure.
The root وري primarily means to conceal or hide something, especially fire or embers. It also refers to something being ignited or coming forth, like fire from wood.
The root خفي (khfy) primarily means to be hidden, concealed, or secret. It can refer to something that is not apparent or known, whether intentionally or unintentionally.
The root جنب (jnb) primarily refers to the side of a person or object, extending from the armpit to the flank. It can also mean a general side, region, or quarter.
Qismah refers to a division or apportionment of things into shares. It can also mean a portion or share itself, similar to qism. The term implies something that has been divided or distributed.
The root هزأ (hzA) primarily means to mock, scoff, or ridicule someone. It can also mean to break something, or, less commonly, to kill camels with cold or to excite a riding beast.
The root ع-ص-ي primarily means to disobey, rebel, or act contrary to a command or will. It implies resistance and opposition, often against authority or divine instruction.
The root كفي (kfy) primarily means to suffice or be sufficient. It conveys the idea of something being enough or adequate for a purpose, fulfilling a need, or being sufficient for someone.
The root جنح primarily means to incline or lean towards something, physically or metaphorically. It describes a bird contracting its wings to descend, the sun setting, or night approaching.
The root مَرَر primarily signifies passing by, going through, or continuing. It can also denote bitterness or something that is firm and strong, like a twisted rope.
The root شمس primarily describes a day being sunny or the sun being intense. It also refers to a horse refusing to be ridden, becoming rebellious, or a woman abstaining from men.
The root 'عرش' (Ersh) primarily refers to a shaded structure, like a booth or shed, often made of natural materials.
The root برك (brk) primarily refers to a camel's breast, the part it rests on when kneeling. It also describes a herd of camels lying down.
The root "Hyn" refers to a period of time, often vague, but can be specific like 40 years or a glance. It can mean an appointed term, a year, or the time of an event.
The root فَتَحَ (fataḥa) primarily means "to open" something, like a door or a conduit. It extends to "conquer" a land, "explain" a problem, or "reveal" a secret.
The root بطل (bTl) primarily means something becoming false, vain, useless, or null, like a deed or an assertion. It also describes a person becoming idle or unoccupied.
The root شرب (shrb) primarily means "to drink" any liquid, often by gulping. It can also mean to be satisfied with drinking or, paradoxically, to be thirsty.
The root "wrth" primarily means "to inherit." It refers to receiving property, status, or even spiritual legacy from an ancestor or predecessor.
The root Q-R-N relates to things that are paired or connected. It can refer to a generation of people, an equal in age, or the side of the head where horns might grow.
The root ريب (ryb) primarily signifies causing disquiet or agitation of mind, leading to doubt or suspicion.
The root بلو (blw) primarily means to test or try, often with the intent of revealing something.
The root غفل (gfl) signifies being unaware, heedless, or negligent.
The root طوف (Twf) primarily means to go or walk around something, like circumambulating the Kaaba during Hajj.
The root "sbq" primarily means to precede, outstrip, or be before someone or something, in various contexts like racing, speech, or actions.
The root سخر (s-kh-r) primarily means to compel or constrain someone or something to work without compensation.
The root كره (krh) signifies dislike, displeasure, or disapproval. It is the opposite of desire, contentment, or love.
The root عهد (Ehd) signifies a command, compact, or promise, often implying an obligation or agreement. It also refers to protection or safeguard, like a covenant of security.
The root QTE generally means to cut or sever. It can describe being cut off from a journey due to inability or misfortune, or speech being cut short.
The root Hdth primarily signifies novelty or innovation, especially in religious matters, often implying disapproval. It also refers to accidents, misfortunes, or calamities.
The root لعن (lEn) can refer to the base or lower part of a palm tree's raceme. This is a less common meaning, found in specialized lexicon entries.
The root ذرر primarily refers to scattering or dispersing small particles, like dust or grain.
The root "jhd" primarily means to strive, labor, or exert oneself to the utmost. It also conveys the sense of being severely affected, distressed, or fatigued by something.
The root أوي primarily means to betake oneself to a place for lodging, shelter, or refuge. It implies seeking protection or a dwelling, often with the sense of returning or resorting to a safe haven.
The root "ترك" (taraka) primarily means to leave, abandon, or forsake something or someone, either intentionally or by necessity. It can also mean to neglect or omit.
The root ق ر ر primarily signifies settling, becoming firm, or remaining in a place.
The root نسي primarily means to forget, to omit, or to neglect something, often unintentionally. It can also imply leaving something behind or abandoning it.
The root هوي (hwy) primarily signifies falling or descending, often implying a downward motion or a plunge.
The root مرأ (mrA) is primarily linked to the word مَرْءٌ (marʾun), which means 'a man' or 'a human being.
The particle "إلى" (ila) primarily signifies "to" or "until," marking the end of an extent in space or time. It can also mean "with" or "in addition to," indicating accompaniment.
The root "dhnb" primarily refers to a tail, like an animal's. It can also metaphorically describe the end or last part of something, such as the "tail of a story" or the "end of a valley.
The root نكر (nkr) primarily means to ignore, not know, or be unacquainted with something or someone. It can also mean to deny or disacknowledge, especially a right.
The root طغي primarily signifies exceeding bounds, whether in water overflowing or a person transgressing limits.
The root Q-W-Y primarily signifies strength, power, and ability. It describes something or someone becoming strong, firm, or mighty.
The root جبل (jbl) primarily refers to a large company or multitude of people. It can also denote a nation or people.
The root سُلْطَانٌ (sultan) primarily denotes strength, power, and authority, often referring to dominion or sovereign rule. It can also signify a clear proof, evidence, or argument.
The root فلح (f-l-ḥ) primarily means to cleave or split, like iron or a head. It also refers to tilling land.
A "shi'ar" is a distinguishing mark or sign, like a battle cry or banner, used to identify groups.
The root "bHr" primarily refers to a large body of water, whether a sea or a great river.
The root بَدَلَ (badala) means to change or alter. It can refer to changing a thing's form or quality while its substance remains the same, or changing it by substituting one thing for another.
The root خشي primarily signifies fear, particularly a reverential fear or awe of God. It implies being humbled and submissive due to this fear, often leading to avoidance of what is feared.
The root يسر (ysr) primarily conveys the meaning of ease, facility, and convenience, standing in direct contrast to difficulty (عُسْرٌ).
The root م ل أ primarily means "to fill." It can describe filling a vessel, satisfying the eye with beauty, or being filled with emotions like fright.
The root "fwq" primarily means to be above, excel, or surpass. It also describes the rising of wind from the chest (hiccuping) or a gasping at death.
The root طعم (TEm) primarily means "to eat" or "to taste." It can refer to consuming food or drink, or simply experiencing its flavor. The word طعام (ta'ām) means "food.

The root جوب (jwb) primarily means to make a hole, cut, or hollow out something, like cutting a rock or a garment. It also extends to traversing or cutting through a space, such as a land or darkness.
The root S-D-D primarily means to turn away, hinder, or obstruct. It implies blocking a path or preventing access, often with the sense of averting someone from a goal or purpose.
The root حزن (Hzn) primarily means to be or become sorrowful, sad, or grieved. It can also mean to cause someone to grieve.
The root أثم (Athm) primarily means to sin or commit a crime, doing what is unlawful. It also describes God reckoning something as a sin or punishing someone for it.
The root ف-ص-ل (fa-ṣa-la) means to separate, divide, or distinguish. It can refer to weaning a child, making a clear decision in a dispute, or a boundary separating lands.
The root حفظ (Hfzh) means to keep, preserve, guard, or take care of something. It also refers to memorizing, especially the Quran, and being mindful of God's ordinances.
The root S-R-R primarily signifies concealment and secrecy, like hiding something within oneself or in a designated place.
The root H-L-L primarily signifies untying, loosening, or solving something. It also conveys the idea of descending, alighting, or becoming permissible.
The root حشر (Hshr) primarily means to gather or collect people, often implying driving them together or compelling them to emigrate.
The root "zyn" means to adorn, beautify, or grace something or someone. It can refer to physical ornamentation or the embellishment of actions or speech.
The root وَذَرَ (wadara) means "to leave, let alone, or cease from.
The root S-D-R primarily refers to the front part of something, especially the chest or breast, which can metaphorically represent the mind or inner self.
The root صبح (SbH) primarily refers to the morning, specifically from sunrise to noon, or even from midnight to noon. It is the opposite of evening (مساء).
The root عجل (Ejl) primarily means to incite or cause someone to hasten or be quick. It can also mean to precede someone or something, or to do something hastily before its proper time.
The root دبر (dbr) primarily means to turn one's back, retreat, or go backward. It can describe physical movement, the decline of affairs, or the ending of a period like day or prayer.
The root سوع (swE) primarily refers to a "sāʿah," meaning an hour or an indefinite short period of time. In the Quran, it often denotes the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing its suddenness.
The root SrT refers to a road or way. It is also the name of a bridge over Hell, sharper than a sword and thinner than a hair, which people must cross to reach Paradise.
The root DEf primarily means "the like of a thing." Over time, it evolved to mean "the like and more," implying an unlimited addition or multiplication.
The root "Tyb" (طيب) primarily means something is good, pleasant, pure, or clean. It can describe delightful tastes or smells, a cheerful or willing state of mind, or something becoming lawful.
The root كرم (krm) signifies generosity, nobility, and high esteem. It describes something as honorable, precious, or excellent, whether referring to people, animals, land, or possessions.
The root FSD means to make something bad, corrupt, or unsound.
The root QDM relates to putting something forward, advancing it, or causing it to precede. It can mean to offer, present, or prepare something beforehand.
The root "Ajl" primarily signifies an appointed term or period, like a deadline for a debt or the waiting period for divorced women.
The root عقل (Eql) primarily means to withhold or restrain. It describes binding a camel's leg, paying blood money (as camels were bound for payment), or a medicine binding the bowels.
The root نفع (nfE) means to profit, benefit, or be useful to someone or something. It can also describe a remedy being good or beneficial for a disease.
The root ع د د primarily means to count, number, or reckon. It also conveys the idea of preparing something for a specific purpose or time, and can refer to a number or quantity itself.
The root ت-ح-ت primarily denotes "beneath," "below," or "under," contrasting with "above." It can be an adverb or a noun, often indeclinable when its associated noun is suppressed.
The root ندي primarily signifies moisture, dew, or dampness.
The root "Hml" primarily means to bear, carry, or convey. It extends to a woman becoming pregnant, a tree bearing fruit, or taking on responsibility for a debt.
The root "rwH" primarily describes wind-related phenomena: a day being windy, or a place becoming cool and airy.
The root خَبَرَ (khabra) primarily means to know something deeply, especially its inner state. It also signifies trying or testing something to gain knowledge or experience.
The root نسو (nsw) refers to a vein or nerve, often associated with the thigh and leg. It's known as the sciatic vein/nerve, and the term can also denote sciatica or hip-gout.
The root دَارٌ (dār) primarily denotes a house, mansion, or any place of abode, often including a courtyard.
The root "Drb" primarily means to strike or beat. It can also mean to set up (a tent), coin (money), seal (a writing), or impose (a tax).
The root ف س ق (fsq) primarily means to go forth from something in a bad or corrupt manner, like a date coming out of its skin.
The primary meaning of QRY relates to collecting or gathering water, often in a basin or reservoir.
A "bayt" is primarily a tent, often made of hair or wool, varying in size and number of poles. It also refers to any house, dwelling, or chamber, including structures of clay or stone.
The root ن-ه-ي primarily signifies prohibition, forbidding, or restraining someone from doing something. It also conveys the idea of reaching an end or limit, as in the "end" of a matter.
The root فري (fry) describes a lamb or its skin, or a kid's skin, being roasted until its upper parts become dried up. This term is found in Q. 3.
The root ذَهَبَ primarily means "to go" or "to depart." It can also mean to go away with something, to remove it, or to cause it to disappear.
The root Swb primarily means to descend or go down. It also signifies hitting a target, like an arrow, or an event befalling someone.
The root زكو (zkw) primarily means increase, augmentation, and purity, often with divine blessing. It also signifies purification, good conduct, and religious service.
The root ظنن primarily means to think, imagine, or suppose something to be true, often with an element of doubt or uncertainty.
The root مَسَسَ primarily means to touch, feel, or handle something with the hand. It can also imply affecting or reaching something, like an affliction or a blessing.
The root "zhhr" primarily refers to the back, contrasting with the belly. It can metaphorically describe having a large or small household, or being forgotten/neglected.
The root ردد primarily means to return, repel, or send back. It encompasses the idea of turning something back, whether physically or metaphorically, and can also imply repetition or reconsideration.
The root فتن (ftn) primarily means to burn or melt something, like gold, to purify or test it.
The root عود (Ewd) primarily means "to return" or "to revert to a state." It can also signify "to become" or "to begin.
The root غيب (ghyb) primarily means to be absent, hidden, or concealed. It describes something out of sight or beyond perception, like the setting sun or a person who has journeyed away.
Ziyādah (زيادة) means an increase, addition, or augmentation. It refers to something extra or superfluous. For example, "letters of augmentation" are letters added to a root word.
The root سحر (sahar) primarily refers to the time just before daybreak, the last part of the night.
The root قضي primarily means to decide, judge, or decree something. It also conveys the sense of completing, finishing, or fulfilling a matter, often with an element of finality or inevitability.
The root موه (mwh) primarily means to coat something, like silvering or gilding.
The root خسر (khsr) primarily means to lose, suffer loss, or be deceived, often in trade or personal acquisitions like health or intellect. It can also mean to err, go astray, or perish.
The root كسب (kasaba) primarily means to collect or gain, acquire, or earn something, like wealth.
The root "tlw" primarily means to follow, whether physically or figuratively, like the moon following the sun.
The root ذوق (dhwq) primarily means "to taste" food or drink. By extension, it signifies perceiving or experiencing something, not limited to the tongue.
The root وَكَلَ (wakala) primarily means to rely upon someone, confide in them, or submit oneself to them.
The root "عَيْنٌ" (Eyn) is a homonym with over a hundred meanings, seventeen of which appear in the Quran. Its primary meaning is "the eye," the organ of sight.
The root عرف (Erf) primarily means 'acknowledgment' or 'confession.' It also signifies 'goodness,' 'beneficence,' or 'what is deemed good/approved.
The root هلك (hlk) primarily means to perish or be destroyed. It can also describe a gradual perishing due to grief.
The root يمن (ymn) primarily refers to the right side or the south. It also signifies a covenant or oath, often made by God.
The root جرى primarily signifies flowing, running, or moving swiftly, like water or a ship. It also denotes the passage of time or events, and the act of happening or occurring.
The root WFY primarily means to fulfill, complete, or perform something fully and perfectly.
The root بعث (b-ʿ-th) primarily means to remove restraint, enabling free action. It signifies sending someone or something, rousing or exciting, and awakening from sleep.
The root رضو (rDw) primarily means to be pleased, content, or satisfied with someone or something. It can also mean to approve, like, or choose.
The root مَتَاعٌ (matāʿ) refers to anything useful or advantageous, like goods, household items, or provisions. It can also denote enjoyment or the necessities of life.
The root جَرَمَ (jrm) primarily means "to cut" or "to cut off," especially in the context of harvesting fruits like dates or shearing wool. It also signifies "to gain" or "to earn.
The root حمد (Hmd) means to praise, commend, or speak well of someone, often for their volitional actions or qualities. It implies admiration, honor, and sometimes humility.
The root "skn" primarily means to be still, quiet, or at rest after motion. It also conveys the idea of trusting or relying on something for peace of mind, and dwelling or inhabiting a place.
The root فَرَقَ (faraqa) means to separate, distinguish, or divide.
The root "رجل" (rijl) primarily refers to the leg or foot of humans and animals. It can also denote a part or portion of something, like half of a roasted sheep or a pair of saddlebags.
The root وَحْد (wHd) primarily means "one" or "single," signifying something without subdivision. It's often interchangeable with أَحَدٌ, especially for God, but with distinct usage patterns.
The root عَلَى (ʿalā) primarily denotes superiority, both physical (e.g., "upon the roof") and abstract (e.g., "a debt is upon him").
The root توب (twb) primarily means to return. When a person "returns" (تَابَ), it signifies repenting from sin, expressing regret, and turning back to God.
The root شكر (shkr) primarily means to thank, be grateful, or acknowledge beneficence.
The root بأس (bAs) primarily conveys the idea of strength, courage, and severity, often in the context of war or adversity. It can also denote distress, misfortune, or a state of being in need.
The root ضَرَر primarily signifies harm, injury, or damage, whether physical or moral. It encompasses causing detriment to someone or something, and experiencing such adversity.
The root W-H-Y primarily signifies a swift, secret, and subtle communication or indication.
The root كَلَمَ (kalam) refers to speech, words, or discourse, whether little or much, singular or plural. It encompasses spoken language, sayings, and even a grammatical sentence.
The root حُرْمَةٌ (ḥurmah) signifies something forbidden, sacred, or inviolable. It also denotes reverence, respect, and honor due to a person or thing.
The root وَجْه (wjh) primarily refers to the 'face' or 'countenance,' often symbolizing the whole self, as in 'resigning oneself to God.

The root زَوْج (zawj) primarily means one of a pair or a couple, or a sort/kind of thing. It can refer to a husband or wife, a consociate, or a like/fellow. In arithmetic, it signifies an even number.
The root عَرَضَ (ErD) primarily means "to be or become broad/wide." It also signifies something appearing or becoming apparent, especially from afar, or an event befalling someone.
The root غني primarily signifies self-sufficiency and independence from others. It conveys being rich, content, and having no need. It also relates to dwelling or residing in a place.
The root ألم (Alm) signifies experiencing pain or aching. It describes a state of suffering, whether of a person or a body part like the belly or head.
The root "بلغ" (balagha) primarily means to reach, attain, or arrive at a destination, time, or state. It encompasses the idea of reaching the utmost point or full maturity, whether physically (e.g.
The root Q-L-L primarily means to be or become little, small, or few. It can also refer to making something little, or to a small quantity or number.
The root 'Eqb' primarily refers to the heel of a human foot. It extends to mean the end or last part of something, like the end of a month or the consequence of an action.
The root نجو (njw) primarily means to escape or be safe. It can also describe swiftness, outstripping others, or, in a more crude sense, voiding excrement or breaking wind.
The root شطن (shTn) refers to anything excessively proud, rebellious, or distant from truth. It can describe humans, jinn, or even certain serpents.
A *muqriʾ* can refer to a menstruating woman, or one who has become pure after menstruation. It also denotes someone who teaches others to read or recite, especially the Qur'an.
The root سوي (swy) primarily means to make even, level, or straight. It also conveys the idea of completing, perfecting, or fashioning something in due proportion.
The root "wld" primarily refers to birth and offspring. A "walīd" is a newborn, infant, or young child. It can also denote a boy, youth, or servant, especially one born into servitude.
The root MWL primarily refers to "wealth" or "property." It encompasses anything one owns, from currency to animals like camels, which were a significant part of Arab wealth.
The root أخو (akhw) primarily means "brother," referring to a male sibling by birth or fosterage. It can also metaphorically mean a friend, companion, or associate.
Sujud primarily means to be humble/submissive, often involving bending down. In prayer, it's prostrating with the forehead on the ground.
The root ليل (layl) primarily refers to night. Related phrases include "daughters of the night" for wishes and anxieties, and "son of the night" for a thief or traveler.
The root AHd primarily means "one" or "first." It's often interchangeable with "wahid" but has specific uses. For God, "Ahad" means "The One, the Sole," emphasizing indivisibility.
The root كَيَّفَ (kayyafa) and its derivatives, used by Muslim theologians, mean to specify something by its quality. These terms were formed by analogy, not directly heard from ancient Arabs.
The root "laysa" (ليس) is a verb of negation, meaning "is not." It functions like "kana" (كان), making the subject nominative and the predicate accusative.

The root HBB primarily conveys the meaning of love, affection, and being beloved. It also encompasses the idea of producing seeds or grains, and by extension, becoming pregnant or having a full udder.
The root نفق (nfq) primarily relates to something being in demand, selling well, or becoming brisk, like a market.
The root خلد (khld) signifies permanence or eternity, as in "Paradise" (دار الخلد). It also refers to a type of bracelet or earring.
The root "dyn" primarily means to be obedient, abased, or submissive. It also signifies following a religion, especially Islam. Interestingly, it can also mean to be disobedient or mighty.
The root بَعْض (bED) primarily means "some" or "a part/portion" of something, whether small or large. It can refer to people or things.
The root "sbH" relates to declaring God's absolute perfection and freedom from any imperfection. "SubhanAllah" means "Glory be to God," expressing wonder and praise, acknowledging His transcendence.
A "ṣāḥib" is a companion, associate, or friend. It also means a lord, master, or owner of something. In the Quran, it refers to companions in Paradise or Hell, and recording angels.
The root صلو (Slw) primarily means to pray, supplicate, or perform the ritual prayer (ṣalāh). When God or angels "pray" for someone, it means to bless, have mercy, or magnify them.
The root أذن (Adhn) primarily refers to the ear, an organ of sense. It can also metaphorically describe a person who is a good listener or who readily believes what is said to them.
The root ب-غ-ي primarily means to seek or desire something, often with an implication of exceeding bounds or acting unjustly. It can denote transgression, rebellion, or seeking something wrongfully.
The root "qarab" primarily means to be or become near. It can refer to physical proximity, closeness in rank, or family relationship.
