The root فضل (fDl) primarily signifies excess, superabundance, or superiority, often implying a positive quality like grace or bounty, especially from God.
The root "Sbr" primarily means to confine or restrain. This can apply to oneself, leading to the meaning of patience or endurance, especially in the face of adversity.
The root أجر (Ajr) primarily means recompensing or rewarding someone for their actions. It also refers to hiring someone or letting something for hire, like a house.
The root شَدَدَ primarily conveys the idea of strengthening, making firm, or binding tightly. It implies intensity, severity, or becoming hard and robust.
The root "wjd" primarily means "to find" or "to discover," encompassing physical, intellectual, and sensory perception. It can also mean "to become rich" or "to be angry with someone.
The root أكل primarily means "to eat" or "to consume." It extends to various metaphorical uses, such as consuming wealth, time, or even defaming someone.
The root فِعْل (fiʿl) refers to a deed, action, or motion, encompassing any origination or effect produced by an agent. It's a broad term for what has become apparent due to a motive.
The root نَهَرَ (nahara) primarily describes water flowing strongly, like a river, or blood gushing. It also means to dig a river channel.
The root HSB primarily means to number, count, or calculate. It also conveys the sense of thinking or supposing something to be true.
The root رَجَعَ primarily means "to return" or "go back" to a place, state, or action. It can also signify repentance, retracting a statement, or taking back a gift.
The root "أبو" (abw) primarily means "father" or "ancestor." It has various declensions and plural forms, including "آباء" (ābāʾ).
The root أمم primarily signifies heading towards a place or person with an intention. It also relates to leadership, being in front, or being a model to be followed.
Rizq (رزق) refers to provisions or sustenance, especially from God. It encompasses both material things like food and immaterial blessings like knowledge.
The root جزي primarily means to recompense or reward, often for good or evil deeds. It implies a return or requital for actions, whether positive or negative.
The root يدي (ydy) primarily refers to the hand, signifying power, possession, or a gift. It can also denote a side, direction, or a means by which something is accomplished.
The root دَخَلَ primarily means "to enter" or "go in," the opposite of "to exit." It can refer to entering a physical space, joining a group, or starting an action.
The root خ و ف primarily means "to fear" or "be afraid." It can also mean "to know" or "to think," as seen in Quranic verses like "if a woman fears ill-treatment from her husband.
The root نذر (ndhr) primarily means to make a vow or impose something as obligatory upon oneself, often to God. It can also mean to dedicate a child to religious service.
The root "nzhr" primarily means to look at or towards something with one's eye. It can also mean to consider or investigate something intellectually, or to face something.
The root خَلَف (khlf) primarily means to come after, follow, or succeed someone or something. It also conveys the sense of being a substitute or replacing what was lost.
The root سأل primarily means to ask, inquire, or question. It also encompasses the idea of begging or requesting something, often with a sense of seeking information or a favor.
The root طوع (TwE) signifies submission, obedience, and willingness. It describes someone who acts voluntarily, not under compulsion, and is compliant or tractable.
The root "b-sh-r" primarily means to strip or pare something, revealing its underlying surface. This can refer to skin, the ground, or even a mustache.
The root "Awl" primarily means to return or revert to an original state, source, or result. It can describe things decreasing, thickening (like milk or oil), or an affair reaching a certain outcome.
The root ر و د (rwd) conveys gentleness, slowness, or a leisurely manner. It can describe walking softly or acting patiently.
Ahl refers to the people of a house, town, or country, and a man's family or cohabitants. It can also mean one's kinsfolk, followers, or those who share a religion or profession.
The root Q-D-R relates to measuring, proportioning, and determining. It can mean to compute the quantity of something, to make a garment to measure, or for God to decree or ordain.
The root Q-T-L, beyond its common meaning of "to kill," can also mean "to know something thoroughly." It implies a deep, complete understanding, as if one has mastered the knowledge of that thing.
The root شهد (shhd) refers to witnessing, observing, or being present. A "shahid" is a witness, one who testifies to what they've seen or know, or someone who is present.
The root جَمْع (jmE) signifies collecting or gathering. It refers to a collection, assembly, or multitude of people or things.
The root عظم (Ezhm) primarily means "to be great in bone," then metaphorically "to be great" in general, whether physically or intellectually.
The root "slm" primarily conveys safety, security, and freedom from imperfections or evils.
The root نعم (nEm) primarily signifies a benefit, favor, or blessing from God, encompassing boons, bounties, and grace. It also denotes ease, plenty, and welfare, often contrasted with hardship.
The root دَنَا (danā) means to be or become near, to approach. It can refer to physical proximity, time, or even kinship.
The root وَعَدَ (waʿada) means "to promise," encompassing both good and evil. When used for good, it's a promise; for evil, it's a threat.
The root L-Q-Y primarily signifies meeting or encountering, whether intentionally or by chance.
The root نصر (nSr) primarily means to aid, assist, or strengthen someone, especially against an enemy or injustice. It also conveys the sense of making someone victorious or avenging them.
The root بصر (bSr) relates to mental perception, understanding, and insight, often contrasted with physical sight. It also signifies knowledge, firm belief, and constancy in religion.
The root "dwn" primarily describes something low, inferior, or beneath, whether in status, quality, or physical position. It can also mean "nearer than" or "before" in terms of proximity or sequence.
The root "mwt" primarily means "to die," the opposite of living.
Shirk (شِرْكٌ) means sharing or partnership, like in land or marriage. It also refers to a share or portion.
The root S-D-Q primarily means to speak the truth, to be veracious, or to prove true. It encompasses sincerity in words, actions, and intentions, contrasting with falsehood.
The root غَيْر (ghayr) means "other than" or "not." It is used to qualify nouns, often governing the following noun in the genitive case.
The root مَثَلٌ (mathal) signifies a description through comparison, often used for important or remarkable states.
The root B-N-Y primarily signifies building, constructing, or erecting something, often with the sense of raising it up.
The root نَبَأَ (nbA) primarily means to utter a low sound or bark. It also conveys meanings of being exalted, assaulting, or going forth from a land.
The root سوأ (swA) primarily means to be or become evil, bad, or unseemly. It can also mean to displease, grieve, or vex someone.
The root كبر (kbr) signifies greatness, age, or importance. أَكْبَرُ means greater/greatest in body, rank, or age. It can also mean older/oldest.

The root "قلب" (qlb) primarily means to alter, change, or invert something, turning it upside down or inside out. It can refer to physical actions like turning over bread or earth, or examining goods.
The root "tbE" primarily means to follow, go after, or pursue. It can imply literally following someone's footsteps, or figuratively following their actions, guidance, or even pursuing a debt.
The root خَرَجَ (khrj) primarily means to go or come out, to issue forth. The form أَخْرَجَ (akhraja) means to make something go out, to expel, extract, or produce it.
The root كثر (kthr) signifies abundance, whether in quantity, number, or frequency. It describes something as much, many, numerous, or copious.
The root "smE" primarily relates to hearing. It can mean the act of hearing, the faculty of hearing (the sense of the ear), or the ear itself.
The root سبل (sbl) primarily means "to let loose or hang down," often referring to garments dragging on the ground.
The root حيي primarily signifies life, living, and being alive.
The root ضلل primarily means to go astray, deviate from the right path, or err, whether intentionally or unintentionally. It can also imply being lost or perishing.
The root صلح (SlH) means to make something good, right, or sound. It encompasses rectifying, correcting, improving, or restoring something to a proper state.
The root "nwr" primarily refers to "fire" (نَارٌ), its flame, and heat. It can metaphorically signify war, evil, or even counsel. It also denotes a brand mark on camels, used for identification.
The root HSN generally means "good," "beautiful," or "pleasing." It describes something intrinsically good, like faith, or extrinsically good, like fighting for a cause.
The root خَيْر (khyr) signifies "good" in various forms: moral, physical, or beneficial. It can refer to wealth, horses, or general well-being.
The root دعو (daʿaw) primarily means to call, invite, or summon. It also encompasses praying or supplicating to God, whether for good or against someone.
The root H-K-M primarily means to prevent or restrain someone from evil or undesired actions. It also refers to curbing a horse or controlling events.
The root `عند` (ʿinda) primarily functions as an adverb of place and time, meaning "at," "near," "with," or "in the presence of.
The root ملك (mlk) primarily means to possess or own something, often with exclusive rights and the ability to exercise authority over it.
The root جَنّ (jann) primarily means to cover, conceal, or hide. It refers to something that is veiled or becomes dark, like the night.
The root غفر primarily means to cover or conceal. From this, it extends to God covering sins, meaning to forgive or pardon them.
The root W-L-Y primarily signifies being near, close, or following. It extends to concepts of guardianship, protection, friendship, and authority, often implying a close relationship or succession.
The root "khlq" primarily means to measure or proportion something, like a hide for sewing.
The root بَعُدَ primarily means to be or become distant, remote, or far off. It can also signify perishing or dying. In some contexts, it expresses improbability or reaching an extreme degree.
The root أَمَرَ (amara) primarily means "to command" or "order." It can also signify "to have authority" or "to govern.
The root وقي (wqy) primarily means to protect, guard, or preserve something from harm or danger. It encompasses the idea of shielding oneself or others, and being cautious or wary.
The root أخر (Akhr) primarily means "last," "aftermost," or "end," contrasting with "first." It refers to the final part of something, like the end of a day or life.
The root "Akhdh" primarily means "to take" or "to seize." It can also mean "to receive," "to accept," "to take possession of," or "to take away.
The root عبد (Ebd) primarily refers to a male slave or servant. It also denotes a worshipper of God or other deities, and can simply mean a human being.
The root نزل primarily signifies descent, like milk into an udder. It also means to lodge or host someone, providing refuge.
The root كذب primarily means "to lie" or "utter a falsehood," whether intentionally or not.
The root ج-ي-أ primarily means "to come" or "to be present." It can refer to physical arrival, the occurrence of events, or even bringing something forth.
The root HQQ primarily signifies truth, reality, and certainty. It denotes that which is established as true, right, or due.
The root ذَكَرَ (dhakara) primarily means to remember or recall something, especially after forgetting. It also encompasses the act of mentioning, telling, or relating something verbally.
The root هدي (hdy) primarily means to guide or lead someone on the right path, often with the implication of showing the way or directing.
Nafs (نفس) refers to the soul, spirit, or vital principle, often contrasted with rūḥ (روح). It can also mean a thing's self or essence.
The root كَتَبَ primarily means "to write." It also signifies "to prescribe, appoint, or ordain," especially by God, making something obligatory.
The root قبل (qbl) primarily means to face or come forward.
The root "ظلم" (ẓalam) primarily means to put something in a wrong place or to transgress proper limits. It encompasses doing wrong, acting unjustly, or causing loss.
The root رَأَى primarily means to see with the eye or perceive with the mind.
The root "جعل" (jaʿala) is a versatile verb meaning to make, create, or appoint.
The root عَمَل (Eml) refers to an intentional action or deed, often implying effort or difficulty. It's more specific than a general "act" (فِعْل) and is typically attributed to animate beings.
The root أنس (Ans) primarily refers to mankind, often contrasted with jinn. It also signifies a close, chosen friend or companion.
The root عذب (Edhb) primarily refers to motes or particles floating on water, or the green substance (طُحْلُب) found in water.
The root "smw" relates to "ism" (name). An ism is a sign or word that conveys knowledge of a thing, distinguishing it. It's derived from "samawtu" or "sumuww," meaning to elevate or make known.
The root K-L-L primarily signifies weariness, dullness, or becoming blunt, like a sword losing its sharpness.
A *rasūl* is primarily a messenger, one sent with a message, often an apostle of God. The word implies a continuous relaying of tidings, like camels following one another.
The root "ywm" primarily refers to a period of time, often a day from sunrise to sunset, or from dawn to sunset. It can also denote an event or accident, a day's journey, or a battle/conflict.
The root "أرض" (ArD) primarily refers to the earth, ground, or land. It can denote the planet, a country, or a piece of soil.
The root شَيَأ primarily means a "thing" or "something." It refers to an entity, object, or matter, whether concrete or abstract, that exists or is conceived. It can also denote a state or affair.
The root "byn" has two opposite meanings: separation and union. It can refer to the distance between things or people, or the state of affairs between them, whether good or bad.
The root كفر (kfr) primarily means to cover or conceal something. From this, it extends to covering up or denying a favor, leading to the meaning of ingratitude.
The root أتي primarily signifies coming, arriving, or bringing something. It can also denote happening, occurring, or being given.
The primary meaning of اِسْم (ism) is a name, or that by which a thing is known. It can also refer to a quality or characteristic that distinguishes something.
The root قوم (qwm) primarily means to stand, rise, or be erect. It extends to undertaking or managing affairs, maintaining someone, or even signifying the establishment of something.
The root أمن (Amn) primarily conveys security, safety, and freedom from fear. It also extends to concepts of trust, confidence, and being trustworthy.
The root "Elm" (علم) primarily means "to know" or "to be acquainted with." It signifies true, certain knowledge, often implying a deeper understanding than mere acquaintance.
The root ر ب ب (rbb) primarily means to be master, owner, or lord. It also conveys the sense of nurturing, rearing, or bringing up something to maturity.
The root "kwn" primarily means "he/it was." It's an "incomplete" verb, meaning it needs a predicate to form a complete thought, like "Zeyd was standing.
The root ق و ل (qawala) primarily means "to say." It can also mean to assert belief, make a sign with a body part, or even to lie.
Allah (اللّٰهُ) is the proper name for the one true God, encompassing all attributes of perfection.
